The government closed schools and educational institutions on March 17 and has extended the closure several times, most recently until November 15."    https://web.archive.org/web/20201122211406/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/11/13/bangladesh-extends-school-shutdown-over-second-covid-19-wave
column12: Targeted: According to the US Embassy Website in Bangladesh as of Nov 11, 2020 https://web.archive.org/web/20201111005505/https://bd.usembassy.gov/covid-19-information/:   "Currently, only certain sectors located within the Wari jurisdiction of the Dhaka South City Corporation are designated as ‘lockdown/containment’ zones. In these areas, the City Corporations will facilitate emergency response services.    Restrictions on Designated Lockdown/Containment Areas:  - Pedestrian and vehicular movements controlled through secured entry/exit points.  - Residents should remain within their homes except for emergencies or for essential needs.  - No indoor dining services allowed. Delivery food service options are available.  - Grocery stores and pharmacies will remain open.  - Residents will be allowed to shop in bazaars only when necessary.  - Residents must work from home.  - Transportation will be suspended. Rickshaws, vans, taxis, auto-rickshaws, and private vehicles are not permitted inside the demarcated areas during the 21-day lockdown.  - COVID-19 tests will be available to residents, and home isolation or institutional isolation will be arranged for patients who test positive.  - Shopping malls, gyms, sports complexes and recreation centres will be closed.  - No public gatherings of any kind are allowed.  - Only people who are ill may go to hospitals.  - Mosques and other places of worship are closed to residents. Only official staff are permitted to enter.  - ATM services will remain open. Banks will operate in a limited capacity.  - Factories in towns will remain closed, but factories and agricultural production-related factories in rural areas can remain operational.  - Agricultural work must be performed under strict health and hygiene regulations."    This information has not changed as of Nov 18, 2020: https://web.archive.org/web/20201122221519/https://bd.usembassy.gov/covid-19-information/      IN GENERAL: Workplace restrictions seem be removed.  Dhaka Tribune: "On October 31, the Cabinet Division sent notices to all public offices of the country, asking them to restrict entry and to refuse service to anyone without a mask. The notice further said masks have been made compulsory for all offices, courts, shopping malls, bazaars, state or government buildings and social events."  source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201122215536/https://www.dhakatribune.com/health/coronavirus/2020/11/02/no-restriction-on-public-movement-to-curb-second-wave-of-covid-19    Nov 12, reuters.com: "“The decision has been taken considering the second wave... column29: Flights from certain countries are banned at this time:    US Embassy, Bangladesh website:  Wayback snapshot Nov 11 2020: https://web.archive.org/web/20201111005505/https://bd.usembassy.gov/covid-19-information/  Updated Nov 18 2020; Wayback snapshot Nov 22, 2020: https://web.archive.org/web/20201122221519/https://bd.usembassy.gov/covid-19-information/    "The Government of Bangladesh has authorized the resumption of limited international commercial flights.  International flights to/from Bahrain, China, India, Malaysia, Maldives, Oman, Qatar, Sri Lanka, Turkey, U.A.E. and the U.K. are permitted to operate.    To avoid the further spread of the COVID-19 pandemic, the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh announced until further notice all international commercial passenger flights from Bhutan, Hong Kong, Kuwait, Nepal, and Thailand shall not be allowed to land at any airport in Bangladesh."    Additionally, most passengers landing in Bangladesh via flights must have a COVID-19 negative certificate irrespective of where their place of departure.    "If international travelers arrive in Bangladesh with COVID-19 symptoms, they will be institutionally quarantined for 14 days.  If international travelers arrive in Bangladesh with no COVID-19 symptoms, they will be required to “home quarantine” for 14 days."

The British government has noted that the UK is amongst some of the few countries where commercial passenger flights have resumed. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201205202636/https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/bangladesh/coronavirus

column32: On 30 March 2020 the government adopted a decree for the provision of support of the local business in relation to the COVID-19 crisis. Under this program the government will cover up to 60% from the insurance income of the employees based on the request of the employer and 60% of the part of the social security contributions due by the employer. The remaining 40% of the employees’ remunerations shall be paid by the employer. The measures will apply in respect of employees whose work has been suspended. In case of part-time work the measures will be applied proportionally in respect of the part of the non-working hours.  The support will be available for sectors directly affected by the crisis including retail, restaurants, tourism and those exhaustively listed in the decree of the Council of Ministers. The measures require the employer to pay the full remuneration to the employees, not to terminate any employees due to reduced workload, headcount reductions and closure of part of the enterprise. column34: On April 10 2020, the Bulgarian National Bank approved the draft Order to defer and settle required liabilities to banks and their subsidiaries. The approved private moratorium provides an opportunity for changes in the repayment schedule of principal and / or interest rates, without changing key parameters of the credit agreement, such as the interest rates already agreed. The instalments may be deferred for up to 6 months, ending on 31 December 2020. The instalments must have been regularly serviced or with a default of no more than 90 days by 1 March 2020.  Customers must explicitly state to their servicing bank that they wish to benefit from the facilities offered.  Three standardized mechanisms are envisaged: (1) Deferral of principal and interest for up to 6 months; (2)  deferral of principal for up to 6 months; (3) applicable to revolving products.  The respective mechanism will be chosen by mutual agreement between the banks and their clients.  [https://web.archive.org/web/20200428130634/https://coronavirus.bg/bg/merki/ikonomicheski]  The full text of the approved order for deferral and settlement of required liabilities to banks and their subsidiaries - financial institutions can be accessed at https://web.archive.org/web/20200428133806/https://www.bnb.bg/bnbweb/groups/public/documents/bnb_pressrelease/pr_20200410_a1_bg.pdf

column36: New socio-economic measures worth BGN 1.162.9 billion were presented by the Prime Minister, after the proposals were finalized earlier today within the Coalition Council. The government's measures are aimed at supporting those fighting in the front lines against the spread of COVID-19 and helping those most affected by the pandemic. The source of expenditures is the national budget, with social measures amounting to BGN 731.5 million and economic ones BGN 431.4 million.    "The goal is to minimize the damage caused by the pandemic in many sectors," said Prime Minister Boyko Borissov.  http://web.archive.org/web/20200730110004/https://coronavirus.bg/bg/news/438    Part of the announced financial package worth ~$699m is intended as an emergency stimulus for the health system and I've included the difference in H4.
column47: "The Prime Minister announced that from August 1, the staff costs of bodies and administrations responsible for pandemic control and the consequences of COVID-19 will be increased by 30%. For front-line employees, the rate for night work is increased. Additional overtime costs in the amount of BGN 92.0 million are envisaged for the structures of the systems of the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Labor and Social Policy, the Ministry of Interior, the National Health Insurance Fund, the National Social Security Institute and others.    An additional BGN 24.6 million is allocated to increase from August 1 the standards for the activities delegated by the state for school and children's health care and health offices. The aim is for the payment to reach the certain levels under the Collective Labor Agreement in the Healthcare sector, as well as the standards in the social sphere (homes for the elderly, homes for the disabled, homes for residential services, day care centers for children, accommodation centers from family type, etc.).    In the next three months, all pensioners will receive BGN 50 per month as a supplement to their pensions, thus a total of 2,121,000 pensioners will be supported. The necessary funds for this amount to a total of BGN 318.3 million.    The funds for subsidies of the medical establishments - commercial companies under Ordinance ? 3 for the medical activities outside the scope of the obligatory health insurance, subsidized by the Ministry of Health, are increased by BGN 17.3 million. The funds are provided to achieve the capacity to serve patients with COVID-19 and to reach the levels of wages to the levels of the Collective Labor Agreement.    It is also envisaged to increase the value of health insurance payments for medical and dental care by an average of 10% to a total of BGN 126.3 million. The aim is to increase the costs of medical staff so as to reach the minimum levels of Collective Labor contract.  Another social measure worth BGN 67.0 million, provided by redirecting funds from European programs, is the provision of a net remuneration of BGN 1,000 to the medical specialists involved in the fight against COVID-19 on the first line until the end of 2020.  More than 38,000 people will benefit from the measure worth BGN 8.0 million, representing assistance for the use of basic tourist services for domestic tourism worth BGN 210 for persons who have directly carried out or are carrying out activities related to treatment. , preventing the spread and / or overcoming the effects of COVID - 19."    http://web.archive.org/web/20200730110004/https://coronavirus.bg/bg/news/438

column55: On 4 December, the National Plan for Vaccination against COVID-19 was adopted. No deliveries yet received so coded as 0    The vaccine for Bulgarian citizens will be completely free and voluntary, according to the Prime Minister.     There are two conditions for immunization - expressed desire and informed consent.    "We are fulfilling our commitment and adopting the National Plan on time. The country is ready and logistically to meet the first delivery of vaccines and, without wasting any time, to start immunization, which will be completely free and voluntary," said Borissov.    The Minister of Health reports that the necessary freezers for storing the vaccines are already available, as well as specialized transport for their delivery in the country. Angelov emphasized that the vaccination plan specifies the phases that determine which groups of the population and in what order will be immunized against the new virus - medical teams, social and pedagogical staff, the elderly over 65 years, patients with chronic diseases."    Parliament has backed the government plan to take part in an EU scheme and get vaccine shots from Pfizer, AstraZeneca and Sanofi.    Vaccines will be administered only with the permission of the European regulator. To ensure that sufficient quantities of COVID-19 vaccines are provided in the country as soon as possible, they will be delivered centrally through a joint EU public procurement mechanism.    The government expects to receive 12-13 million doses at a total cost of about EUR 250 million (USD 304 million).    https://web.archive.org/web/20201214235545/https://coronavirus.bg/bg/news/938    https://web.archive.org/web/20201214235756/https://coronavirus.bg/bg/news/939    https://web.archive.org/web/20201215015622if_/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-bulgaria-vaccines/bulgaria-prepares-for-covid-19-vaccines-as-death-rates-spike-idUSKBN28E0Z3
column62: On 4 December 2020, The Council of Ministers adopted the national vaccination plan against COVID-19. The plan consists of 5 vaccination phases, with priority determined by epidemiological and ethical criteria.     Phase 1   Doctors, nurses, paramedics (Medical staff for outpatient and inpatient medical examinations assistant, medical specialists in health care, dentists, pharmacists, assistant pharmacists and other assistant staff.)    Phase 2  Users and staff of social institutions, educational specialists and staff of farms mink.    Phase 3  Employees involved in maintaining the functioning of the core for public life activities, such as those in the water sector.     Phase 4  Elderly people over and over 65 years of age and accompanying persons chronic diseases due to the more severe course of the disease and the higher risk of developing complications and death, incl. immunocompromised or persons with secondary immune deficiencies.    Phase 5  Vulnerable groups of the population due to the high epidemiological risk of infection associated with their conditions and lifestyle.    ** "Vulnerable groups of the population due to the high epidemiological risk of infection associated with their conditions and lifestyle" is coded as "clinically vulnerable." & "Employees involved in maintaining the functioning of the core for public life activities" is coded as "frontline/essential workers (when subcategories are not specified."    https://web.archive.org/web/20210108212501/https://www.mh.government.bg/media/filer_public/2020/12/04/natsionalen_plan_za_vaksinirane_sreshchu_covid-19_v_republika_blgariia.pdf?fbclid=IwAR05c9oKWEgAmlFuATZ9-1CJS-CWi0IG_Ft0f6lt6c3Ed3hJHimYcrRc23I     https://web.archive.org/web/20210110162320/https://bntnews.bg/news/nacionalniyat-plan-za-vaksinirane-sreshtu-covid-19-u-nas-shte-proteche-v-5-fazi-1085877news.html     https://web.archive.org/web/20210124121655/https://www.gov.bg/bg/prestsentar/novini/premierat-borisov-priehme-natsionalniya-plan-za-vaksinirane-sreshtu-COVID-19-i-sme-gotovi-za-parvite-dostavki-na-vaksini

column34: The Bahrain government paid the electricity and water bills for Bahraini individuals and companies for April, May, and June. column12: “Emergency Powers (Covid 19)(No. 1) Order, 2020…shall come into force at 9:00 a.m. on the 20th day of March, 2020”  “For every island and cay of the Commonwealth of The Bahamas, for a period of eleven days commencing the 20th day of March, 2020 —  (1) All establishments, institutions, businesses, offices, stores and organizations shall suspend operations to the general public except for the following —” The following include essential workplaces such as “wholesale or retail grocery stores and Farmers’ Markets from 6:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.” Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20210103131054/https://higgsjohnson.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/3.-Emergency-Powers-COVID-19-No.-1-Order-2020.pdf
column15: “Emergency Powers (Covid 19)(No. 1) Order, 2020…shall come into force at 9:00 a.m. on the 20th day of March, 2020 and shall expire at 9:00 a.m. on the 31st day of March, 2020.”  It is required that public events are cancelled because all non-essential “establishments, institutions, businesses, offices, stores and organisations shall suspend operations to the general public”. Workplaces that can continue to operate include pharmacies, gas stations, and “wholesale or retail grocery stores and Farmers’ Markets”. Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20210103131054/https://higgsjohnson.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/3.-Emergency-Powers-COVID-19-No.-1-Order-2020.pdf
column18: “Emergency Powers (Covid 19)(No. 1) Order, 2020…shall come into force at 9:00 a.m. on the 20th day of March, 2020 and shall expire at 9:00 a.m. on the 31st day of March, 2020.”  “No person shall host or attend —   (i) a private party which includes any person from outside of the immediate household of the house occupant”  “(iii) a wedding which hosts ten or more persons other than the bride, bridegroom, official witnesses and the marriage officer”  “(vi) a funeral, except ten members of the immediate family and at least one officiant and the essential mortuary staff”   Weddings are the exception to gatherings of 10 or more people who don’t live in the same household being prohibited. Therefore, C4 is being coded a 4 as the typical, and most stringent, measure is restrictions on gatherings of 10 people or less.  Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20210103131054/https://higgsjohnson.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/3.-Emergency-Powers-COVID-19-No.-1-Order-2020.pdf

column32: “We set aside $4 million for disbursement through the Department of Social Services, for food assistance and social support for displaced workers directly impacted by COVID-19. column12: The Office of The Prime Minister’s “Emergency Powers (COVID 19) (No.2) Order, 2020” published on March 23rd stated that “Every non-essential establishment, or business shall remain closed”. column27: “On March 23, the Prime Minister of The Bahamas announced additional measures in response to the global COVID-19 pandemic”, effective March 24. “Under these orders all domestic inter-island traffic by air or boat within The Bahamas is also temporarily banned.  This includes refueling, stopping and anchoring, passing through or innocent passage. Although the emergency orders allow vessels to depart The Bahamas directly for the United States, there are no exceptions for anyone, whether Bahamian citizen, resident, or foreigner, to circumvent the restrictions on inter-island movement.” Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20201115205856/https://bs.usembassy.gov/health-alert-u-s-embassy-nassau-the-bahamas-april-6-2020/
column29: “On March 23, the Prime Minister of The Bahamas announced additional measures in response to the global COVID-19 pandemic.  These additional measures include closing all airports and seaports of The Bahamas to incoming international flights carrying visitors, effective March 24 (including private airports).  These entry restrictions were broadened March 27 to include all incoming passengers, including Bahamian citizens and residents. Under these orders all domestic inter-island traffic by air or boat within The Bahamas is also temporarily banned.  This includes refueling, stopping and anchoring, passing through or innocent passage. Although the emergency orders allow vessels to depart The Bahamas directly for the United States, there are no exceptions for anyone, whether Bahamian citizen, resident, or foreigner, to circumvent the restrictions on inter-island movement.  If local authorities do not permit you to transit due to these restrictions, you must shelter in place.” Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20201115205856/https://bs.usembassy.gov/health-alert-u-s-embassy-nassau-the-bahamas-april-6-2020/
column34: Published on March 24th: “The Central Bank of The Bahamas has arranged with domestic banks and credit unions to provide a 3-month deferral against repayments on credit facilities for businesses and households that were negatively impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic.” Source: https://archive.vn/zeyKI   Also, Bahamas Power and Light announced on March 24th that “it will immediately suspend disconnections until March 31 as thousands of Bahamians are forced to stay home to prevent the spread of the coronavirus (COVID-19).” Source: https://archive.vn/tIwCT
column58: “Emergency Powers (Covid 19)(No. 2) Order, 2020…shall come into force at 9:00 a.m. on the 24th March, 2020 and shall expire at 9:00 a.m. on the 31st March.  “A curfew is imposed every day for twenty-four hours except as provided herein or as may be approved by the Commissioner of Police.”  “Every non-essential establishment, or business shall remain closed except for the following —  (a) wholesale or retail grocery stores and Farmers’ Markets from 6:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., the first two shopping hours to be reserved for seniors, disabled persons and essential workers”  This policy protects the elderly because it limits their potential exposure to Covid-19 while carrying out essential activities. column32: “The $20 million allocated by the Government for MSMEs [small and medium sized businesses] will ensure that all businesses who qualify have the support they need to protect their livelihoods and the families represented by their workforce.”    “EXPANDED UNEMPLOYMENT ASSISTANCE FOR SELF-EMPLOYED WORKERS”  “A national crisis, such as the pandemic before us today where, due to forces entirely beyond their control, thousands of self-employed people who rely on the flow of cruise ship and stopover visitors, are now unable to make a living over the next few weeks. As such, the Government has partnered with NIB to design a temporary programme that will provide weekly payments of $200 to persons who meet the eligibility criteria, for a period of up to 8 weeks. That is, an eligible person can receive up to $1,600 over the 8-week period.”  “On the 26 of March 2020, NIB launched its new online application process for the Government Funded Unemployment Assistance for COVID-19.”   “Self-employed persons, outside of the tourism trade, are also facing the complete loss of income and the challenge of meeting their financial obligations. They too will receive a benefit payment of $200 per week for the length of the quarantine period which at present will go at least until April 8th.”    “As a reminder, for businesses that make less than $3 million annually, the SBDC is currently providing support through a Business Continuity Loan Programme. I am pleased to announce, however, that as an additional measure, specifically targeted towards payroll assistance, the Government is offering a grant of between $2,000 to $20,000 for MSME’s who qualify for a Business Continuity Loan to assist with payroll. We are allocating an additional $5 million to finance this initiative.”  Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20210109164845/https://higgsjohnson.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/13.-Update-on-the-Fiscal-and-Economic-Impact-of-COVID-19-1.pdf     Also, “Other unemployed individuals are able to apply for unemployment benefits under NIB’s existing unemployment benefit scheme which provides payments for a period of 13 weeks.” Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20210109165308/https://home.kpmg/xx/en/home/insights/2020/04/the-bahamas-government-and-institution-measures-in-response-to-covid.html

column36: On March 30th, the “Minister of Finance presents Parliament with update on Government’s stimulus measures in response to COVID-19”   “We set aside $4 million for disbursement through the Department of Social Services, for food assistance and social support for displaced workers directly impacted by COVID-19.”  “The Ministry of Finance is budgeting an initial $5.9 million to cover these additional self-employed persons impacted by the current lockdown.”  “The SBDC also rolled out the Government’s $20 million COVID-19 response last week, targeted to provide loans to small businesses, ranging from $5,000 to $300,000.” This is being grouped with the March 30th announcements; the date the $20 million COVID-19 response was rolled out, the week prior to the week beginning March 30th, wasn’t found.  “The Ministry of Finance is allocating $1.8 million to support the Family Islands specifically to be used for any COVID-19 related expenditure.”   Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20210110134442/https://bahamasbudget.gov.bs/2020/news-centre/latest-news/2020/03/30/over-120-million-pledged-covid-19-social-support-and-economic-stimulus/

column36: The “May 2020 Budget Communication” by the Minister of Finance, The Hon. K. Peter Turnquest, stated the monetary value of different fiscal stimuli to date.  “To illustrate the extent of our initiatives, as of mid-May, the National Insurance Board (NIB) paid out some $6.2 million for the Government funded unemployment assistance program.”  “Under the standard Unemployment Benefit Scheme, NIB also paid out $28.8 million in benefit claims to those laid off as a result of the virus. This has covered just over 26,000 people since the end of March.”  “The Department of Inland Revenue approved 44 companies, who collectively benefitted from some $5.7 million in tax credits and deferrals.”   Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20210110134600/https://bahamasbudget.gov.bs/budget-communication/   “Budget Communication FY 2020/2021” “From Crisis to Opportunity” “Presented to the House of Assembly by the Hon. K. Peter Turnquest, M.P., Deputy Prime Minister & Minister of Finance on Wednesday, 27th May 2020” This includes announced spending, for the future.  “The spike in unemployment across the world has left millions of people without their primary source of income. In The Bahamas, this has created hardship in our communities. More than 55,000 people have already filed for unemployment benefits and assistance with the National Insurance Board, representing over 30 percent of our workforce.   ? This Administration stands for the dignity of work. Our bond with citizens is defined by partnership, not paternalism. Therefore, in our plan, we allocate over $120 million to continue and expand the Tax Credit/Tax Deferral program to provide cash directly to businesses to fund their payroll expenses to help keep people employed.   ? Our values also demand that no Bahamian is left hungry, or without shelter and care. In our plan, we allocate over $85 million to ensure the social safety net is strong enough and wide enough to protect the wellbeing of each and every vulnerable Bahamian and resident.”  “Economic Support Measures for COVID-19 Fallout”  $48 million for continued unemployment assistance for persons who remain dislocated.   $17 million in increased social welfare spending to provide expanded food assistance through the Government’s food voucher initiative, as well as to support the expansion of other social programs at the Ministry of Social Services.   “$30 million to expand the business support and continuity loan program for Bahamian entrepreneurs and small businesses.”  Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20210110134645/https://bahamasbudget.gov.bs/media/filer_public/35/3c/353cac9d-265c-40ba-b930-5b08769667c0/2020-21_budget_communication_-_final_1-compressed.pdf

column45: On September 7th, The Ministry of Health “put out a call for individuals interested in joining the government’s contract tracing pool of workers.” “A free online Contact Tracing Course, in collaboration with the University of The Bahamas, has been made available for all those interested, the ministry advised in its Friday COVID-19 update. “The Contact Tracing Strike Force of the Ministry of Health is determined to identify every case and every contact,” the statement said.” “In the first wave of COVID-19 cases in The Bahamas, officials said 62 volunteers were recruited and 76 health staff re-assigned to carry out contact tracing on New Providence, Grand Bahama, and the Family Islands.” Source: https://archive.vn/8hesG

column32: KPMG’s “The Bahamas Government and institution measures in response to COVID-19” was last updated on September 9th, and states:  “Self employed tourism workers who remain unemployed; NIB contributors who are under 35 years old, who were unemployed during the COVID-19 shutdown but did not meet the contribution threshold to receive a benefit; and individuals who have maxed out their 13-weeks of eligibility under the ordinary NIB unemployment benefit are eligible for a 13-week extension of B$150 per week.”   13 weeks from September 9th takes us to December 9th. column9: On August 31st, it was announced “Monday, October 5, 2020 is the targeted date for the opening of public and private schools throughout the archipelago. The Hon. Jeffrey Lloyd, Minister of Education (MOE) in a report to the nation, announced that a substantial increase in the infection rate of the novel coronavirus in New Providence and other Family Islands, has forced the Department of Education to engage in more urgent planning and considerations. Schools were previously scheduled to open on September 21, 2020.”  The Minister of Education, “emphasized that in New Providence, Abaco and Eleuthera, schools will have a virtual format while schools in Grand Bahama and other Family Islands will offer face-to-face classes.” Source: https://archive.vn/9i0u2 It was confirmed again, on October 7th, in an address by the Prime Minister Dr Hubert Minnis, that “schools on New Providence and Abaco, may only proceed via virtual means. column62: Priority list updated on 30 December 2020:    The plan is to prioritise vaccination of target groups of people age 16 as follows:    Target group 1: People at especially high risk (vulnerable people; excluding pregnant women)  Target group 2: Healthcare professionals with patient contact/carers for people at especially high risk  Target group 3: Close contacts (household members) of people at especially high risk  Target group 4: People in communal facilities with an increased risk of infection and outbreaks (for example homes for the handicapped).  Given that as vaccination starts there are not sufficient doses of vaccine available, further prioritisation is necessary within target group 1.  The following people are to be given access to vaccinations first:  People age 75 and over  People with chronic diseases of the highest risk, regardless of their age    After that come:  People aged between 65 and 74  People under 65 and people with chronic diseases who have not yet been vaccinated    Following people in target group 1, the vaccination will be offered to people in target groups 2, 3 and 4 in that order. In due course adults who are not in target groups 1 to 4 will also be able to have the vaccination.    https://web.archive.org/web/20201231115345/https://www.bag.admin.ch/bag/en/home/krankheiten/ausbrueche-epidemien-pandemien/aktuelle-ausbrueche-epidemien/novel-cov/impfen.html

column58: As early as March 18,  Ix-Chel Poot, the Executive Director of the National Council of Ageing (statutory government body) stated the following on national TV:  "One of the first things that we want families to take seriously is that if you have been ill or been contact with some who has been ill is to practice social distancing. As we can see with the experience internationally the coronavirus is deadly for people sixty plus. We are looking at practicing social distancing. You can keep in contact with your older persons via phone, text. Or putting in place the measures in your home to maintain good hygiene. Even keeping up with the hand washing and the disinfecting. And if the older person in your home has an underlying health condition to ensure that his health condition is under control, diabetes, hypertension and that they have the medication that is necessary on hand. We are also stressing that if the older person in you care shows any signs or symptoms to contact the Ministry of Health hotline because there is no time to see what it will develop in that older person.”    Moreover, the National Council for Aging started a registration drive to identify every elder in need, partly so that they can receive additional support such as food assistance (in order to not put them at risk because they have to go buy groceries).    https://web.archive.org/web/20200319163249/https://edition.channel5belize.com/archives/200087  https://web.archive.org/web/20210205180000/https://www.facebook.com/plustvbelize/videos/252374795888128/

column43: Belmopan. March 25, 2020. The Ministry hereby provides a report on an initial mapping exercise in San Pedro Town, Ambergris Caye. column32: 22 June The Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) informed that it has approved a loan of US $12 million for Belize to support the implementation of the COVID-19 Unemployment Relief Program. The loan program will provide protection for the vulnerable population affected by the COVID-19 crisis. Specifically, it will provide cash transfers for a period of 12 weeks to currently unemployed individuals, formerly working in the informal or formal sectors, particularly but not solely in tourism, and who are not on the rosters of other cash transfer programs. The crisis caused by COVID-19 has hurt local income and consumption.  IADB source:http://archive.vn/aqHEr Media Source: http://archive.vn/tw6on  Money has been given to the government as a loan and therefore becomes part of the governments funds, so believe it counts as government supporting income. US$12 million divided by 26,500 individuals is $452. The national statistics office digest on labour statistics reports a median monthly income of $1,134 for Sept 2019 [https://web.archive.org/web/20200430151354/http://sib.org.bz/wp-content/uploads/LabourForce_2019-09.pdf].   Therefore, the support offered is less than 50% of median income.

column36: COVID19- FISCAL PLAN. The current actions being taken as part of the Ministry of Finance COVID-19 - Fiscal Plan are as follows: -To provide financing to supplement reduced revenues, the Ministry is taking the necessary action to secure emergency liquidity lines of credit with local financial institutions. The required discussions have been held with all relevant parties, to gain the necessary approvals, including an associated $150 million increase in the debt ceiling. These facilities will be used only when it is absolutely necessary. The Ministry will provide additional funding for the Department of Financial Assistance to further assist Bermuda’s unemployed. -Lower priority expenditures will be curtailed to ensure that spending needed for COVID-19 matters can be maintained. To that end, over the next 3 months Government will: -Delay the start of any capital projects that have not commenced; Institute an immediate freeze on posts that are not required to address COVID 19 or to protect Bermuda’s national interests; -Continue the ban on non-essential government travel; and -Reduce all discretionary spending, including training, materials and supplies, clothing and uniforms etc".   Archived Source: /web/20200402182725/https://www.gov.bm/articles/covid-19-fiscal-plan

column58: The meeting facilitators recommended that visits to Long Term Care Facilities by members of the public, at this point, should be restricted to end of life care visits only and that these visitors should be screened before they enter the facility. It was suggested that other means of communication should be explored to encourage connectedness during this time.    Prevention measures should also be taken to stop respiratory germs from entering the facilities and from spreading within the facilities. These include: encouraging sick employees to stay home, posting signs at the entrance describing visitor restrictions, and ensuring that sick leave policies allow employees to stay home if they have symptoms of respiratory infection.    Finally, a recommendation was made that protocols for cleaning procedures, staff self-screening and visitor screening, hand and respiratory hygiene should be enhanced while daily staff and resident screening should be conducted.    https://archive.vn/lRpKw

column32: Applications open March 25 for COVID-19 Unemployment Benefit, which the Minister of Labour announced on March 23. column29: "Visitors must present a copy of the pre-departure PCR COVID-19 negative test result to health officers on request and a copy of the Travel Authorization form.  Travelers arriving at the airport will undergo a mandatory non-contact temperature check.  Residents and visitors will undergo PCR COVID-19 testing at the L.F. Wade International Airport and quarantine at home or in their room at their accommodation until results are ready (turnaround time is approximately 24 hours in most cases, though results may take longer depending on arrival time). Residents (including work permit holders) who do not have a pre-departure negative PCR COVID-19 test result must quarantine for eight days after arrival. They will not be tested on day four, but they will be tested on day eight and will be released from quarantine with a day eight negative results. You will still have to test on day 4, day 8, and day 14.  The location and time of each of your tests will automatically be booked for you, so please do not book separate appointments. You will receive email reminders 24 hours before each test. column29: As of this Friday, December 4th, a pre-arrival test must be taken within five days before arriving in Bermuda. All travellers – including returning students – are subject to mobile quarantine restrictions on their movements and activities, until they receive a negative Day 14 COVID-19 test result. http://web.archive.org/web/20201214232216/https://www.gov.bm/articles/covid-19-update-minister-health-remarks-1-december-2020     The Ministry developed ‘mobile quarantine’ as a means by which newly arriving travellers could be ‘free to roam’ if they had both a negative pre-arrival test and a negative test on arrival at the airport. The “Ten Tips for Mobile Quarantine During COVID-19” states, for example, that travellers cannot attend events with large groups of people, they must stay away from crowded places and they need to exercise outside and not in a gym or with a sports team. As part of mobile quarantine, all travellers are required to be tested on Day 4, Day 8 and Day 14 of their stay. If a traveller does not have a negative pre-arrival test, that person has to quarantine until a Day 8 negative test result. http://web.archive.org/web/20201214234331/https://www.gov.bm/articles/ministerial-statement-update-covid-19-public-health-guidance-december-2020

column55: Bermuda has two sources for procuring vaccines against COVID-19.  Bermuda will be supplied with 9,000 doses of the Pfizer vaccine and they will arrive on our shores in the first week of January 2021.   The second vaccine source is through Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance Geneva, which is administering the COVID-19 Vaccine Global Access Facility (the “COVAX Facility”). Bermuda has joined the COVAX Facility, and has purchased enough doses to cover 20% of our population. The leading vaccines likely to be received by Bermuda are those by AstraZeneca and Moderna. The timeframe for receipt of these vaccines through the COVAX Facility is not yet settled.  http://web.archive.org/web/20201215000755/https://www.gov.bm/articles/ministerial-statement-covid-19-vaccine-bermuda

column43: Covid-19 Testing:    The designated government agency regulating COVID-19 testing in Bolivia is the Servicio Departamental de Salud (SEDES).  There are 9 branches of SEDES in the 9 Departments of Bolivia.  First step is to contact SEDES for evaluation at 800-10-2930.  The two available tests are the Quick Test and the CRP test.  The test can be done through SEDES or at a private Hospital or Lab.  In either case, the price for the Quick Test averages in: US$ 50.00 and the CRP test price averages in: US$ 135. column32: Law no. 14.020 institutes the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program. The new law originates from Provisional Measure 936, issued by the government in early April. The program provides for the granting of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit to workers who have reduced working hours or a suspended contract, and also emergency assistance for intermittent workers with a formalized employment contract, under the terms of the provisional measure. The value of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit will be based on the calculation of the monthly amount of unemployment insurance to which the employee would be entitled. In the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  I - in the event of a reduction in working hours and wages, it will be calculated by applying the percentage of the reduction to the calculation basis; and  II - in the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  a) equivalent to 100% (one hundred percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  b) equivalent to 70% (seventy percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716181745/http://www.in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/lei-n-14.020-de-6-de-julho-de-2020-265386938  http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182541/https://www.gov.br/economia/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/publicacoes/boletins/covid-19/timeline/julho/7-de-julho-de-2020    No official declaration on the amount of the measure was mentioned. However, to guarantee the payment of the so-called Emergency Job and Income Preservation Benefit (BEm), the federal government will have to invest between R $ 26.1 and R $ 52.6 billion, according to an analysis by the Independent Tax Institution (IFI) of the Senate. column32: Law no. 14.020 institutes the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program. The new law originates from Provisional Measure 936, issued by the government in early April. The program provides for the granting of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit to workers who have reduced working hours or a suspended contract, and also emergency assistance for intermittent workers with a formalized employment contract, under the terms of the provisional measure. The value of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit will be based on the calculation of the monthly amount of unemployment insurance to which the employee would be entitled. In the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  I - in the event of a reduction in working hours and wages, it will be calculated by applying the percentage of the reduction to the calculation basis; and  II - in the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  a) equivalent to 100% (one hundred percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  b) equivalent to 70% (seventy percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716181745/http://www.in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/lei-n-14.020-de-6-de-julho-de-2020-265386938  http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182541/https://www.gov.br/economia/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/publicacoes/boletins/covid-19/timeline/julho/7-de-julho-de-2020    No official declaration on the amount of the measure was mentioned. However, to guarantee the payment of the so-called Emergency Job and Income Preservation Benefit (BEm), the federal government will have to invest between R $ 26.1 and R $ 52.6 billion, according to an analysis by the Independent Tax Institution (IFI) of the Senate.   Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182524/https://www2.senado.leg.br/bdsf/bitstream/handle/id/574054/NT44.pdf  Link:http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182552/https://www12.senado.leg.br/noticias/materias/2020/07/06/uniao-investira-ate-r-53-bi-para-compensar-reducao-de-salario-e-jornada-avalia-ifi

The Federal Government has extended deadlines for the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program for another two months. According to the decree, the maximum term for the proportional reduction agreement of the working day and salary, which was 90 days, will now be 120 days. The term for the temporary suspension of the contract, which was 60 days, also changes to 120. For employees with intermittent employment contracts, the decree establishes the payment of an emergency benefit of R $ 600.00 for another month, counting from the closing date of the three-month period, for employees with formalized employment contracts until April 1, publication date of the PM creating the program. column32: Law no. 14.020 institutes the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program. The new law originates from Provisional Measure 936, issued by the government in early April. The program provides for the granting of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit to workers who have reduced working hours or a suspended contract, and also emergency assistance for intermittent workers with a formalized employment contract, under the terms of the provisional measure. The value of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit will be based on the calculation of the monthly amount of unemployment insurance to which the employee would be entitled. In the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  I - in the event of a reduction in working hours and wages, it will be calculated by applying the percentage of the reduction to the calculation basis; and  II - in the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  a) equivalent to 100% (one hundred percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  b) equivalent to 70% (seventy percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716181745/http://www.in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/lei-n-14.020-de-6-de-julho-de-2020-265386938  http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182541/https://www.gov.br/economia/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/publicacoes/boletins/covid-19/timeline/julho/7-de-julho-de-2020    No official declaration on the amount of the measure was mentioned. However, to guarantee the payment of the so-called Emergency Job and Income Preservation Benefit (BEm), the federal government will have to invest between R $ 26.1 and R $ 52.6 billion, according to an analysis by the Independent Tax Institution (IFI) of the Senate.   Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182524/https://www2.senado.leg.br/bdsf/bitstream/handle/id/574054/NT44.pdf  Link:http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182552/https://www12.senado.leg.br/noticias/materias/2020/07/06/uniao-investira-ate-r-53-bi-para-compensar-reducao-de-salario-e-jornada-avalia-ifi

column32: Law no. 14.020 institutes the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program. The new law originates from Provisional Measure 936, issued by the government in early April. The program provides for the granting of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit to workers who have reduced working hours or a suspended contract, and also emergency assistance for intermittent workers with a formalized employment contract, under the terms of the provisional measure. The value of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit will be based on the calculation of the monthly amount of unemployment insurance to which the employee would be entitled. In the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  I - in the event of a reduction in working hours and wages, it will be calculated by applying the percentage of the reduction to the calculation basis; and  II - in the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  a) equivalent to 100% (one hundred percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  b) equivalent to 70% (seventy percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716181745/http://www.in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/lei-n-14.020-de-6-de-julho-de-2020-265386938  http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182541/https://www.gov.br/economia/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/publicacoes/boletins/covid-19/timeline/julho/7-de-julho-de-2020    No official declaration on the amount of the measure was mentioned. However, to guarantee the payment of the so-called Emergency Job and Income Preservation Benefit (BEm), the federal government will have to invest between R $ 26.1 and R $ 52.6 billion, according to an analysis by the Independent Tax Institution (IFI) of the Senate.   Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182524/https://www2.senado.leg.br/bdsf/bitstream/handle/id/574054/NT44.pdf  Link:http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182552/https://www12.senado.leg.br/noticias/materias/2020/07/06/uniao-investira-ate-r-53-bi-para-compensar-reducao-de-salario-e-jornada-avalia-ifi

column32: Law no. 14.020 institutes the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program. The new law originates from Provisional Measure 936, issued by the government in early April. The program provides for the granting of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit to workers who have reduced working hours or a suspended contract, and also emergency assistance for intermittent workers with a formalized employment contract, under the terms of the provisional measure. The value of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit will be based on the calculation of the monthly amount of unemployment insurance to which the employee would be entitled. In the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  I - in the event of a reduction in working hours and wages, it will be calculated by applying the percentage of the reduction to the calculation basis; and  II - in the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  a) equivalent to 100% (one hundred percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  b) equivalent to 70% (seventy percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716181745/http://www.in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/lei-n-14.020-de-6-de-julho-de-2020-265386938  http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182541/https://www.gov.br/economia/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/publicacoes/boletins/covid-19/timeline/julho/7-de-julho-de-2020    No official declaration on the amount of the measure was mentioned. However, to guarantee the payment of the so-called Emergency Job and Income Preservation Benefit (BEm), the federal government will have to invest between R $ 26.1 and R $ 52.6 billion, according to an analysis by the Independent Tax Institution (IFI) of the Senate. column32: Law no. 14.020 institutes the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program. The new law originates from Provisional Measure 936, issued by the government in early April. The program provides for the granting of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit to workers who have reduced working hours or a suspended contract, and also emergency assistance for intermittent workers with a formalized employment contract, under the terms of the provisional measure. The value of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit will be based on the calculation of the monthly amount of unemployment insurance to which the employee would be entitled. In the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  I - in the event of a reduction in working hours and wages, it will be calculated by applying the percentage of the reduction to the calculation basis; and  II - in the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  a) equivalent to 100% (one hundred percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  b) equivalent to 70% (seventy percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716181745/http://www.in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/lei-n-14.020-de-6-de-julho-de-2020-265386938  http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182541/https://www.gov.br/economia/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/publicacoes/boletins/covid-19/timeline/julho/7-de-julho-de-2020    No official declaration on the amount of the measure was mentioned. However, to guarantee the payment of the so-called Emergency Job and Income Preservation Benefit (BEm), the federal government will have to invest between R $ 26.1 and R $ 52.6 billion, according to an analysis by the Independent Tax Institution (IFI) of the Senate. column32: Law no. 14.020 institutes the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program. The new law originates from Provisional Measure 936, issued by the government in early April. The program provides for the granting of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit to workers who have reduced working hours or a suspended contract, and also emergency assistance for intermittent workers with a formalized employment contract, under the terms of the provisional measure. The value of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit will be based on the calculation of the monthly amount of unemployment insurance to which the employee would be entitled. column32: Law no. 14.020 institutes the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program. The new law originates from Provisional Measure 936, issued by the government in early April. The program provides for the granting of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit to workers who have reduced working hours or a suspended contract, and also emergency assistance for intermittent workers with a formalized employment contract, under the terms of the provisional measure. The value of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit will be based on the calculation of the monthly amount of unemployment insurance to which the employee would be entitled. In the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  I - in the event of a reduction in working hours and wages, it will be calculated by applying the percentage of the reduction to the calculation basis; and  II - in the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  a) equivalent to 100% (one hundred percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  b) equivalent to 70% (seventy percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716181745/http://www.in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/lei-n-14.020-de-6-de-julho-de-2020-265386938  http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182541/https://www.gov.br/economia/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/publicacoes/boletins/covid-19/timeline/julho/7-de-julho-de-2020    No official declaration on the amount of the measure was mentioned. However, to guarantee the payment of the so-called Emergency Job and Income Preservation Benefit (BEm), the federal government will have to invest between R $ 26.1 and R $ 52.6 billion, according to an analysis by the Independent Tax Institution (IFI) of the Senate.   Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182524/https://www2.senado.leg.br/bdsf/bitstream/handle/id/574054/NT44.pdf  Link:http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182552/https://www12.senado.leg.br/noticias/materias/2020/07/06/uniao-investira-ate-r-53-bi-para-compensar-reducao-de-salario-e-jornada-avalia-ifi

column32: Law no. 14.020 institutes the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program. The new law originates from Provisional Measure 936, issued by the government in early April. The program provides for the granting of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit to workers who have reduced working hours or a suspended contract, and also emergency assistance for intermittent workers with a formalized employment contract, under the terms of the provisional measure. The value of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit will be based on the calculation of the monthly amount of unemployment insurance to which the employee would be entitled. In the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  I - in the event of a reduction in working hours and wages, it will be calculated by applying the percentage of the reduction to the calculation basis; and  II - in the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  a) equivalent to 100% (one hundred percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  b) equivalent to 70% (seventy percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716181745/http://www.in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/lei-n-14.020-de-6-de-julho-de-2020-265386938  http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182541/https://www.gov.br/economia/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/publicacoes/boletins/covid-19/timeline/julho/7-de-julho-de-2020    No official declaration on the amount of the measure was mentioned. However, to guarantee the payment of the so-called Emergency Job and Income Preservation Benefit (BEm), the federal government will have to invest between R $ 26.1 and R $ 52.6 billion, according to an analysis by the Independent Tax Institution (IFI) of the Senate.   Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182524/https://www2.senado.leg.br/bdsf/bitstream/handle/id/574054/NT44.pdf  Link:http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182552/https://www12.senado.leg.br/noticias/materias/2020/07/06/uniao-investira-ate-r-53-bi-para-compensar-reducao-de-salario-e-jornada-avalia-ifi

The Federal Government has extended deadlines for the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program for another two months. According to the decree, the maximum term for the proportional reduction agreement of the working day and salary, which was 90 days, will now be 120 days. The term for the temporary suspension of the contract, which was 60 days, also changes to 120. For employees with intermittent employment contracts, the decree establishes the payment of an emergency benefit of R $ 600.00 for another month, counting from the closing date of the three-month period, for employees with formalized employment contracts until April 1, publication date of the PM creating the program. column32: Law no. 14.020 institutes the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program. The new law originates from Provisional Measure 936, issued by the government in early April. The program provides for the granting of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit to workers who have reduced working hours or a suspended contract, and also emergency assistance for intermittent workers with a formalized employment contract, under the terms of the provisional measure. The value of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit will be based on the calculation of the monthly amount of unemployment insurance to which the employee would be entitled. In the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  I - in the event of a reduction in working hours and wages, it will be calculated by applying the percentage of the reduction to the calculation basis; and  II - in the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  a) equivalent to 100% (one hundred percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  b) equivalent to 70% (seventy percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716181745/http://www.in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/lei-n-14.020-de-6-de-julho-de-2020-265386938  http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182541/https://www.gov.br/economia/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/publicacoes/boletins/covid-19/timeline/julho/7-de-julho-de-2020    No official declaration on the amount of the measure was mentioned. However, to guarantee the payment of the so-called Emergency Job and Income Preservation Benefit (BEm), the federal government will have to invest between R $ 26.1 and R $ 52.6 billion, according to an analysis by the Independent Tax Institution (IFI) of the Senate.   Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182524/https://www2.senado.leg.br/bdsf/bitstream/handle/id/574054/NT44.pdf  Link:http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182552/https://www12.senado.leg.br/noticias/materias/2020/07/06/uniao-investira-ate-r-53-bi-para-compensar-reducao-de-salario-e-jornada-avalia-ifi

column32: Law no. 14.020 institutes the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program. The new law originates from Provisional Measure 936, issued by the government in early April. The program provides for the granting of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit to workers who have reduced working hours or a suspended contract, and also emergency assistance for intermittent workers with a formalized employment contract, under the terms of the provisional measure. The value of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit will be based on the calculation of the monthly amount of unemployment insurance to which the employee would be entitled. In the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  I - in the event of a reduction in working hours and wages, it will be calculated by applying the percentage of the reduction to the calculation basis; and  II - in the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  a) equivalent to 100% (one hundred percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  b) equivalent to 70% (seventy percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716181745/http://www.in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/lei-n-14.020-de-6-de-julho-de-2020-265386938  http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182541/https://www.gov.br/economia/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/publicacoes/boletins/covid-19/timeline/julho/7-de-julho-de-2020    No official declaration on the amount of the measure was mentioned. However, to guarantee the payment of the so-called Emergency Job and Income Preservation Benefit (BEm), the federal government will have to invest between R $ 26.1 and R $ 52.6 billion, according to an analysis by the Independent Tax Institution (IFI) of the Senate. column32: Law no. 14.020 institutes the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program. The new law originates from Provisional Measure 936, issued by the government in early April. The program provides for the granting of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit to workers who have reduced working hours or a suspended contract, and also emergency assistance for intermittent workers with a formalized employment contract, under the terms of the provisional measure. column32: Law no. 14.020 institutes the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program. The new law originates from Provisional Measure 936, issued by the government in early April. The program provides for the granting of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit to workers who have reduced working hours or a suspended contract, and also emergency assistance for intermittent workers with a formalized employment contract, under the terms of the provisional measure. The value of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit will be based on the calculation of the monthly amount of unemployment insurance to which the employee would be entitled. In the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  I - in the event of a reduction in working hours and wages, it will be calculated by applying the percentage of the reduction to the calculation basis; and  II - in the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  a) equivalent to 100% (one hundred percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  b) equivalent to 70% (seventy percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716181745/http://www.in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/lei-n-14.020-de-6-de-julho-de-2020-265386938  http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182541/https://www.gov.br/economia/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/publicacoes/boletins/covid-19/timeline/julho/7-de-julho-de-2020    No official declaration on the amount of the measure was mentioned. However, to guarantee the payment of the so-called Emergency Job and Income Preservation Benefit (BEm), the federal government will have to invest between R $ 26.1 and R $ 52.6 billion, according to an analysis by the Independent Tax Institution (IFI) of the Senate.   Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182524/https://www2.senado.leg.br/bdsf/bitstream/handle/id/574054/NT44.pdf  Link:http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182552/https://www12.senado.leg.br/noticias/materias/2020/07/06/uniao-investira-ate-r-53-bi-para-compensar-reducao-de-salario-e-jornada-avalia-ifi

column32: Law no. 14.020 institutes the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program. The new law originates from Provisional Measure 936, issued by the government in early April. The program provides for the granting of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit to workers who have reduced working hours or a suspended contract, and also emergency assistance for intermittent workers with a formalized employment contract, under the terms of the provisional measure. The value of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit will be based on the calculation of the monthly amount of unemployment insurance to which the employee would be entitled. In the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  I - in the event of a reduction in working hours and wages, it will be calculated by applying the percentage of the reduction to the calculation basis; and  II - in the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  a) equivalent to 100% (one hundred percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  b) equivalent to 70% (seventy percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716181745/http://www.in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/lei-n-14.020-de-6-de-julho-de-2020-265386938  http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182541/https://www.gov.br/economia/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/publicacoes/boletins/covid-19/timeline/julho/7-de-julho-de-2020    No official declaration on the amount of the measure was mentioned. However, to guarantee the payment of the so-called Emergency Job and Income Preservation Benefit (BEm), the federal government will have to invest between R $ 26.1 and R $ 52.6 billion, according to an analysis by the Independent Tax Institution (IFI) of the Senate.   Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182524/https://www2.senado.leg.br/bdsf/bitstream/handle/id/574054/NT44.pdf  Link:http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182552/https://www12.senado.leg.br/noticias/materias/2020/07/06/uniao-investira-ate-r-53-bi-para-compensar-reducao-de-salario-e-jornada-avalia-ifi

column32: Law no. 14.020 institutes the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program. The new law originates from Provisional Measure 936, issued by the government in early April. The program provides for the granting of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit to workers who have reduced working hours or a suspended contract, and also emergency assistance for intermittent workers with a formalized employment contract, under the terms of the provisional measure. The value of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit will be based on the calculation of the monthly amount of unemployment insurance to which the employee would be entitled. In the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  I - in the event of a reduction in working hours and wages, it will be calculated by applying the percentage of the reduction to the calculation basis; and  II - in the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  a) equivalent to 100% (one hundred percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  b) equivalent to 70% (seventy percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716181745/http://www.in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/lei-n-14.020-de-6-de-julho-de-2020-265386938  http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182541/https://www.gov.br/economia/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/publicacoes/boletins/covid-19/timeline/julho/7-de-julho-de-2020    No official declaration on the amount of the measure was mentioned. However, to guarantee the payment of the so-called Emergency Job and Income Preservation Benefit (BEm), the federal government will have to invest between R $ 26.1 and R $ 52.6 billion, according to an analysis by the Independent Tax Institution (IFI) of the Senate.   Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182524/https://www2.senado.leg.br/bdsf/bitstream/handle/id/574054/NT44.pdf  Link:http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182552/https://www12.senado.leg.br/noticias/materias/2020/07/06/uniao-investira-ate-r-53-bi-para-compensar-reducao-de-salario-e-jornada-avalia-ifi

The Federal Government has extended deadlines for the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program for another two months. According to the decree, the maximum term for the proportional reduction agreement of the working day and salary, which was 90 days, will now be 120 days. The term for the temporary suspension of the contract, which was 60 days, also changes to 120. For employees with intermittent employment contracts, the decree establishes the payment of an emergency benefit of R $ 600.00 for another month, counting from the closing date of the three-month period, for employees with formalized employment contracts until April 1, publication date of the PM creating the program. column32: July 7 - Law no. 14.020 institutes the Emergency Employment and Income Maintenance Program. The new law originates from Provisional Measure 936, issued by the government in early April. The program provides for the granting of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit to workers who have reduced working hours or a suspended contract, and also emergency assistance for intermittent workers with a formalized employment contract, under the terms of the provisional measure. The value of the Emergency Employment and Income Preservation Benefit will be based on the calculation of the monthly amount of unemployment insurance to which the employee would be entitled. In the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  I - in the event of a reduction in working hours and wages, it will be calculated by applying the percentage of the reduction to the calculation basis; and  II - in the event of temporary suspension of the employment contract, it will have monthly value:  a) equivalent to 100% (one hundred percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  b) equivalent to 70% (seventy percent) of the unemployment insurance amount to which the employee would be entitled  Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716181745/http://www.in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/lei-n-14.020-de-6-de-julho-de-2020-265386938  http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182541/https://www.gov.br/economia/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/publicacoes/boletins/covid-19/timeline/julho/7-de-julho-de-2020    No official declaration on the amount of the measure was mentioned. However, to guarantee the payment of the so-called Emergency Job and Income Preservation Benefit (BEm), the federal government will have to invest between R $ 26.1 and R $ 52.6 billion, according to an analysis by the Independent Tax Institution (IFI) of the Senate.   Link: http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182524/https://www2.senado.leg.br/bdsf/bitstream/handle/id/574054/NT44.pdf  Link:http://web.archive.org/web/20200716182552/https://www12.senado.leg.br/noticias/materias/2020/07/06/uniao-investira-ate-r-53-bi-para-compensar-reducao-de-salario-e-jornada-avalia-ifi

column36: July 13 - Banco do Brasil credited the funds corresponding to the second installment of the financial assistance provided for in  Supplementary Law 173/2020 . The amounts will be deposited in the same accounts as the State Participation Fund (FPE) and the Municipality Participation Fund (FPM). A total of R $ 15.038 billion will be deposited for subnational entities. The Complementary Law, signed by President Bolsonaro in March, allows the granting of federal aid of around R $ 60.15 billion to states, municipalities and the Federal District to strengthen actions to combat the new coronavirus. column47: Brazil already has 9,273 ICU beds authorized by the Federal Government to treat exclusively severely or very seriously ill patients with Covid-19. column29: From 29 July, Brazil has officially reopened its borders to international travel, which had been banned since March. However, an additional 30 days ban on the entry of foreigners by land (unless for transit) and sea has been extended.    The borders are open to nationals, residents, and tourists. Non-resident foreigners can enter for a period not exceeding 90 days and must show proof of the purchase of valid health insurance in Brazil with coverage for the entire period of travel. column29: Barbados Ministry of Tourism’s updated travel protocols came into effect on August 3rd.   These protocols state that “persons from High-Risk countries with a valid negative COVID-19 PCR test result will be quarantined at a designated holding hotel or approved villa at their own expense, or free of charge at a government facility, and will be monitored daily for the onset of symptoms. These persons will be quarantined for a period of 14 days with an option to take a second COVID-19 PCR test between 5-7 days after the last test accepted by the Ministry of Health and Wellness. Persons will typically be released once the test result is negative.” “High-Risk: Includes USA, Brazil, India, Mexico, Argentina, Peru, Colombia, South Africa, Indonesia, Philippines and Russia.”  Countries not classified as High-Risk, unless within the “Bubble”, which includes “Saint Lucia, St. Kitts & Nevis, Grenada, Dominica and St. Vincent & The Grenadines”, are required to take a COVID-19 PCR test prior to or on arrival. column52: The Barbados government published the 'Emergency Management (COVID-19)  Protocol (No. 4) Directive, 2020' on 29th October 2020. Measures outlined will apply between the 29th October, 2020 and the 27th March, 2021.    The Protocol specifies that masks must be worn for those in attendance at events including private parties, recreational or competitive sporting events, a banquet, ball or reception, any social event, a meeting of a fraternal society, private or social club or civic association or organization, and political meetings. Masks must also be worn at places of public entertainment, and on public transport.     The government also published the Emergency Management (Covid-19)Churches (No. 5) Directive on 28th October. This Directive stated that masks must be worn at Church, but exceptions are made for those who are officiating, preaching, singing, reading, praying or playing a wind instrument.     https://drive.google.com/file/d/120tlIBURJq4vvzEgG4UR5khtz-N9jxXJ/view

column12: The Barbados government published the 'Emergency Management (COVID-19)  Protocol (No. 4) Directive, 2020' on 29th October 2020. Paragraph 2 of this document states that businesses can operate so long as they follow social distancing policies for staff and customers, provide hand sanitising stations for staff and customers, limit the number of people inside or outside their establishment at any time so that there is at least 6 feet between every individual, make sure that people do not assemble otherwise than for the purpose of transacting business, and follow any other policies that are implemented by the Chief Medical Officer and Covid-19 Protocol Monitoring Unit.    https://drive.google.com/file/d/120tlIBURJq4vvzEgG4UR5khtz-N9jxXJ/view
column15: The Barbados government published the 'Emergency Management (COVID-19)  Protocol (No. 4) Directive, 2020'. Measures outlined will apply between the 29th October, 2020 and the 27th March, 2021.    The Protocol allows any business regulated under the Public Entertainments Act who wishes to reopen to seek the permission of the Covid-19 Protocol Monitoring Unit. This Unit will decide the maximum number of patrons that the business can accommodate and the conditions of operation and any additional protocols required. All those at a place of public entertainment must wear a face mask.    More generally, the Protocol allows events with no more than 500 people to be held. Exceptions can be made and more people can attend if special permission is obtained from the Covid-19 Protocol Monitoring Unit. Attendees must follow strict distancing protocols, wear a face mask and follow any other instructions given by the Covid-19 Protocol Monitoring Unit. Hosts must provide hand sanitiser for all persons in attendance, comply with any instructions given by the Covid-19  Protocol Monitoring Unit, and ensure that physical distancing protocols are observed  by all those in attendance.    https://drive.google.com/file/d/120tlIBURJq4vvzEgG4UR5khtz-N9jxXJ/view
column18: The Barbados government published the 'Emergency Management (COVID-19)  Protocol (No. 4) Directive, 2020' on 29th October 2020. Paragraph 3, sub-paragraph 1 of this document outlines that individuals are able to hold a private party, recreational or competitive sporting event, a banquet, ball or reception, any social event, a meeting of a fraternal society, private or social club, or civic association or organisation, and a political meeting. Paragraph 3, sub-paragraph 2 clarifies that these events cannot be attended by more than 500 people and sub-paragraph 5 states that there must be physical distancing of 1m between attendees, unless they are of the same household. It is mandatory that all persons travelling to Barbados from high and medium risk countries have a negative COVID-19 PCR test done at an accredited or certified facility within three days prior to arrival. Persons arriving from Canada, however, are allowed to be tested on arrival in Barbados, if they are unable to receive their test results in time for departure from their country. All high risk passengers are required to quarantine at a designated hotel or approved villa at their own expense or free of charge at a government facility, up to the time of a second test, which will be four to five days after the first test. At the end of the period, if they test negative, they are discharged from quarantine, but will continue to be monitored for seven days from the time of arrival.    Passengers from medium risk countries are monitored for seven days after arrival and must also undergo a second test within four to five days.    Persons from low risk countries are strongly advised to have a negative test taken within five days of arrival, and those who arrive without it will be tested on arrival.     As of November 3, 50 countries are included in the "High Risk" category     https://web.archive.org/web/20201129214959/https://gisbarbados.gov.bb/blog/50-countries-now-in-covid-19-high-risk-category/

column34: Per latest update from the IMF (November 19, 2020) "The Central Bank of Barbados (CBB) announced a series of measures (effective April 1, 2020) to help support commercial banks and other deposit-taking institution manage the economic fallout from the coronavirus shock.
