column36: "Today, the Honourable Derek Bennett, Minister of Environment, Climate Change and Municipalities, issued a call for applications for the new $23.4 million COVID-19 Stimulus Program for communities in Newfoundland and Labrador.    The COVID-19 Stimulus Program was created to help provide short-term employment and to stimulate economic activity through community projects. The program is targeted at small to medium scale municipal enhancement projects, and COVID-19 municipal upgrades such as repairs, maintenance and minor upgrades to municipal buildings, fire halls, recreation centres, and community property.    One application per community is permitted and approved projects will be based on a 90/10 cost shared ratio with submissions capped at $150,000.    The COVID-19 Stimulus Program encourages municipalities to find opportunities to support health and well-being in infrastructure improvements such as:    Upgrading existing walking trails;  Supporting accessibility, new families and building healthy communities; and  Engaging residents in the revitalization of their communities.  Program guidelines and applications are available online. The deadline to submit an application is December 7, 2020.    The COVID-19 Stimulus Program is in addition to the $27.4 million announced under the Safe Restart Agreement in response to COVID-19. The Federal Government portion of the Safe Restart Agreement is being matched on a 50/50 cost share basis with Provincial Government expenditures retroactive to April 1, 2020."    http://web.archive.org/web/20201123143620/https://www.gov.nl.ca/releases/2020/eccm/1123n03/

column27: "The Honourable Andrew Furey, Premier of Newfoundland and Labrador, today announced temporary changes to the Atlantic Bubble travel protocol.    Effective 12:01 a.m. on Wednesday, November 25, people arriving in Newfoundland and Labrador from within the Atlantic Bubble will be required to self-isolate for 14 days.    Atlantic Bubble travelers will not have to apply for a travel exemption at this time. If anyone within that group has extenuating circumstances making the 14 days of self-isolation impossible, there will be an option to apply for testing to possibly shorten it. Details of this application process will be rolled out over the next few of days.    Updates on these temporary changes related to the Atlantic Bubble will be provided in two weeks."    http://web.archive.org/web/20201126021912/https://www.gov.nl.ca/releases/2020/exec/1123n04/    "The Department of Health and Community Services is advising the public about changes to self-isolation and testing for rotational workers.    Effective Wednesday, November 25, rotational workers from Newfoundland and Labrador who work in Canada and return from a site without an outbreak are now required to wait until day seven of their 14 day self-isolation period to arrange COVID-19 testing.    Once an asymptomatic individual has completed seven days of self-isolation and has received a negative test result, they can visit public places and extended family members. They must wear a mask when interacting with people outside their household bubble. They must not attend mass gatherings or visit crowded spaces. They must not enter a long-term care home, personal care home or assisted living facility for 14 days after they return home, except for exceptional circumstances, such as end of life.    Any adults in a household of a rotational worker are advised that they must wear a mask when interacting with people outside their household bubble for 14 days after the worker returns home. They should avoid mass gatherings and crowded spaces. It is recommended that any adults that reside in a household with a rotational worker in isolation avoid long-term care homes, personal care homes and assisted living facilities, as much as possible.    If the rotational worker or anyone in the household becomes symptomatic, everyone in the household must self-isolate immediately and call 811 to arrange testing.    The public are reminded that this change does not apply to international rotational workers or workers returning from a site with an outbreak. These individuals are required to self-isolate for 14 days on their property. They are unable to leave their property, except to seek medical attention.    Starting Wednesday, November 25, Public Health will be making contact with rotational workers to see if they, or their family, require support in any way during the 14 day self-isolation period and also to provide them with a point of contact for any questions they may have around precautions the family should be taking."    http://web.archive.org/web/20201123213522/https://www.gov.nl.ca/releases/2020/health/1123n10/

column55: (A: Pfizer-BioNtech)    On December 16, 2020, the province began administering the Pfizer-BioNtech COVID-19 vaccine   to healthcare workers in the Central Zone who work in the following areas:  1. column32: The Canada Emergency Response Benefit (CERB) provided financial support to employed and self-employed Canadians who were directly affected by COVID-19.    Eligible were those who met these criteria:    Your work hours were reduced because of COVID-19 (see last checkbox below for more details)  You stopped working because of COVID 19  You were unable to work because of COVID-19, for example because you were taking care of someone  You were paid EI regular or fishing benefits for at least one week of benefits since December 29, 2019 and you used up your entitlement to those benefits    Applicants received $2,000 for a 4-week period (the same as $500 a week), between March 15 and September 26, 2020.    https://web.archive.org/web/20201216154619/https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/benefits/apply-for-cerb-with-cra.html    Have coded as 2F because this does not seem to apply to anyone who does not file taxes- there for not 'informal' workers, so not ALL.

column36: "The Ontario government is moving quickly to put in place a targeted High Priority Communities Strategy that will provide funding to local lead agencies to work in partnership with Ontario Health, public health units, municipalities, and other community partners to deliver key interventions for the province's hardest-hit neighbourhoods.    Evidence shows that racially diverse, newcomer and low-income communities have been impacted more significantly by COVID-19 than others, and they need specific supports as they are facing complex barriers to accessing services and enacting core prevention measures. column9: The Province has outlined it's plans to safely return students to school in September.   Colleges and UPEI remain closed: https://archive.vn/wip/EytX5    The plan includes guidelines for all schools to keep students and staff safe, for example:    Students will work in cohorts, or groups of the same students, as much as possible. Cohorts will distance themselves from other groups to limit exposure to other students.  Classrooms will be configured to support physical distancing. Schools will work to reduce class sizes and when necessary, alternate space such as multi-purpose rooms will be used as classrooms.  Lunch and recess breaks will be staggered, as well as drop-off and pick-up times.  Protocols will be in place to safely move students through the school and reduce congestion in hallways and common areas.  Students and staff will be required to stay home when they are unwell and there will be screening protocols for all people entering a school.  Students will be educated on the importance of physical distancing and hand washing.  Enhanced cleaning protocols will be followed in the school and on the school bus.  To reduce the number of students on buses, parents will be asked to transport their children to and from school whenever possible and buses will be added where necessary.  The plan for September is based on current evidence and recommendations of the Chief Public Health Office. While in-school learning is the preferred model, back-up plans will be in place to move to at-home learning should public health conditions change.  Staff will return to school on September 1 and students on September 8. Orientation on new operational requirements will be held for all staff. Professional learning for teachers will focus on the revised curriculum, online teaching and learning, and student wellness.    https://archive.vn/wip/ajiDY    https://archive.vn/wip/EytX5

column9: When schools K-12 return on 8 September, some levels will be required to wear facemasks. column27: Self-isolation remains required for anyone arriving on the Island from outside of the Atlantic Bubble.   Islanders who are rotational workers (those who travel frequently or routinely outside the Atlantic Bubble (within Canada), spending at least half of their time working outside of Atlantic Canada), do not need to self-isolate or work-isolate. Instead, rotational workers must be tested on a regular basis, monitor for symptoms and follow public health measures such as physical distancing, frequent hand washing and wearing a non-medical mask when physical distancing is not possible. This protocol has been in place since the early onset of the pandemic to balance an acceptable risk of transmission with the need for rotational workers to see their families for the limited time they are home.    Effective October 1, individuals who work outside of the Atlantic Bubble (within Canada) who are required to work outside of their home upon return to PEI can apply to work-isolate, via a self-declaration form that will be available on the provincial website. A letter from the worker’s employer indicating their schedule is required. More information on the work-isolate declaration will be available online early next week.     https://archive.vn/zr1Wg

column36: The Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food, the Minister of Forests, Wildlife and Parks, as well as the federal Minister of Agriculture and Agri-Food, are announcing that the Government of Canada and the Government of Quebec will join forces to financially support Quebec fish farmers in the exceptional context created by COVID-19.  Quebec fish farmers are an important cog in the wheel of food production. The closure of restaurants and the cessation of fishing activities have had a major impact on Quebec's fish farming industry. This situation has led to a drop in the volume of fish purchased from fish farmers and generated a surplus of inventory. The financial contribution from the Quebec government and the federal government is in the order of $408,000 and $612,000 respectively (CAD). So they have made a deliberate decision to vaccinate a third priority group, just not the one the code assumes.       https://web.archive.org/web/20201230062839/https://www.saskatchewan.ca/government/health-care-administration-and-provider-resources/treatment-procedures-and-guidelines/emerging-public-health-issues/2019-novel-coronavirus/covid-19-vaccine/covid-19-vaccine-information

column32: The Canada Emergency Response Benefit (CERB) provided financial support to employed and self-employed Canadians who were directly affected by COVID-19.    Eligible were those who met these criteria:    Your work hours were reduced because of COVID-19 (see last checkbox below for more details)  You stopped working because of COVID 19  You were unable to work because of COVID-19, for example because you were taking care of someone  You were paid EI regular or fishing benefits for at least one week of benefits since December 29, 2019 and you used up your entitlement to those benefits    Applicants received $2,000 for a 4-week period (the same as $500 a week), between March 15 and September 26, 2020.    https://web.archive.org/web/20201216154619/https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/benefits/apply-for-cerb-with-cra.html    Have coded as 2F because this does not seem to apply to anyone who does not file taxes- there for not 'informal' workers, so not ALL.

column41: From 20th March, the Emergency Measures Organisation began publishing Covid-19 updates.    Source:  http://web.archive.org/web/20201129151546if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/read-covid-19-public-updates

column12: As of closing time on 22nd March, all bars must remain closed.    Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20201117170903if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates
column15: On 22nd March, it was announced that gatherings could have no more than 10 attendees. In light of this, public events are not be able to be held. column18: On 22nd March, it was announced that gatherings would be limited and could have no more than 10 attendees. Attendees of these gatherings should socially distance, keeping 2 metres between people. Those with flu-like symptoms, over 65 or with an underlying health condition, or healthcare workers, workers in a healthcare facility or other essential services, should not attend any gatherings.    Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20201117170903if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates
column27: On 22nd March, Yukon’s Chief Medical Officer of Health announced that Yukon residents returning to the province and all visitors must undergo 14 days self-isolation upon arrival, and there would be mechanisms introduced to monitor this.    They also strongly recommended that non-essential travel into and out of Yukon be suspended, same for non-essential travel to Yukon’s rural communities.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201129124348if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates
column43: 22nd March, the Chief Medical Officer for Health stated that travellers returning to Yukon with respiratory systems including a cough, fever, or difficulty breathing, will be asked to call 811 for advice on Covid-19 testing.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201130141404/https://yukon.ca/en/news/yukons-chief-medical-officer-health-provides-update-covid-19-0
column45: On 22nd March, it was announced that Yukon had its first cases of Covid-19. Yukon's Chief Medical Officer of Health in this announcement, emphasised that "Prompt case detection, isolation, and contact tracing in combination with the difficult societal measures that we are all facing, will mean that we can manage COVID-19 in a way that both protects the public and provides high quality care to those who are infected". Such indicates that a contact tracing system is in place.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201201123045if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/covid-19-confirmed-yukon
column58: On 22nd March, Yukon’s Chief Medical Officer of Health requested that Yukoners not attend any social gatherings, even those with fewer than 10 people if they are over 65 or work in healthcare, a healthcare facility or other essential services.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201129124348if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates

column43: A new testing centre was opened in Whitehorse this week, testing those with flu-like symptoms and respiratory issues. column52: Mask-wearing is still not recommended but wearing masks was mentioned in passing on 7th April in the Chief Medical Officer for Health's update, where they mentioned that: "Wearing a non-medical mask such as a homemade cloth mask in the community has not been proven to protect the person wearing it. However, using non-medical mask or facial covering can be an additional measure people can take to protect others around them. It also helps people to be aware of not spreading infection and remember to not touch their face. Wearing a non-medical mask when in public or other settings is not a replacement for following proven measures such as hand washing and safe spacing." column36: The Yukon Business Relief Program was created to support Yukon businesses whose revenue has decreased by 30% by providing them a grant of up to $30,000 CAD a month to support fixed costs between 23rd March and 22nd May. The article referenced states that the Business Relief Program, the Paid Sick Leave Program, the Temporary Support for Events Funding Program (announced on 1st April) as well as changes to the Yukon Nominee Program, all of which have been previously announced, are expected to cost up to $21.7 million CAD ($15,522,446.21 USD). column27: On 17th April, a new Border Control Measures Order came into force which limited those entering the province to Yukon residents, non-resident family members of Yukon residents, those delivering a critical or essential service, those exercising an Aboriginal or treaty right and those transiting through Yukon to a neighbouring jurisdiction (the latter are only allowed to be in Yukon for 24 hours). They state that the advice given will be specific to each contacted individual and their circumstances.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201201112114if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates
column52: April 17, 2020: The Minister of Transport announced measures requiring all air passengers to have a non-medical mask or face covering to cover their mouth and nose during travel. These measures come into effect at noon EDT on April 20, 2020    https://web.archive.org/web/20201119002605/https://www.canada.ca/en/transport-canada/news/2020/04/new-measures-introduced-for-non-medical-masks-or-face-coverings-in-the-canadian-transportation-system.html    https://web.archive.org/web/20201203160259/https://www.mccarthy.ca/en/insights/articles/covid-19-emergency-measures-tracker

column34: On 23rd April, a Ministerial Order under the Civil Emergency Measures Act was signed which extended the deadline for paying property tax from 2nd July to 2nd September for citizens and businesses. column43: Yukon's Chief Medical Officer for Health announced on 24th April that from 27th April, the criteria for those tested for Covid-19 would be expanded.     Those tested for Covid-19 would include those with one of the covid symptoms (fever, chills, cough, difficulty breathing, a sore throat or hoarse voice, headache, runny nose or nasal congestion, unexplained vomiting or diarrhoea, fatigue or muscle aches, or loss of smell or taste) who had travelled outside Yukon in the past 14 days or had close contact with anyone who has travelled outside Yukon.     Even if someone does not have travel history but is symptomatic with fever, cough, or difficulty breathing, they can be tested for Covid-19 as well.    There will also be greater testing in long-term care facilities and the Whitehorse Emergency Shelter.    However, deciding who is tested is ultimately at the health care providers' discretion. They are expected to use their clinical expertise to decide.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201130165725if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/april-24-2020-yukons-chief-medical-officer-health-provides-update-covid-19

column36: On 4th May, it was announced that the aviation sector will receive $3.56 million CAD (2,526,974.25 USD) in support as a result of Covid-19's impact on revenues.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201206161653if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/new-support-available-yukons-aviation-industry

column41: On 8th May, the Yukon Government launched a non-medical Covid-19 information line. The line is described as providing 'Yukon specific information about travel and borders, self-isolation and physical distancing, enforcement, and the various social and economic supports for businesses and families'.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200915234339/https://yukon.ca/en/news/yukon-launches-non-medical-covid-19-information-line

column36: On 11th May, the Government of Yukon announced a new support programme to help tenants who have been affected by Covid-19 pay rent. Tenants who have lost 30% of their income because of Covid-19 and who reside in private non-subsidised market rental housing can apply for the grant to assist with paying rent between April and June. Those who apply may receive 50% of median market rent based on unit size.     The Government of Yukon did not specify how much they expect the programme will cost.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200915234234/https://yukon.ca/en/news/new-support-will-help-tenants-pay-rent-during-covid-19

column9: For Phase 1 of Yukon's plan for lifting Covid-19 restrictions (May 15th - June 30th), schools remain closed. Daycares are allowed to open to children of workers. Summer day camps can now operate along specific guidelines, but they cannot run overnight.    Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20201117155139if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/summary-yukons-plan-lifting-covid-19-restrictions
column18: For Phase 1 of the Yukon plan for lifting Covid-19 restrictions (May 15th - June 30th), gatherings are allowed of 10 people or fewer, indoor or outdoors. Exceptions might be made for funerals and religious services following a public health assessment.      Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20201117155139if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/summary-yukons-plan-lifting-covid-19-restrictions

column27: As a result of shifting to Phase 1 of the Yukon Covid response, guidance on travel to rural communities has been updated. Instead of asking people to avoid non-essential travel to communities, the Chief Medical Officer of Health is now asking people to limit travel to communities.    Quarantine is still required for those travelling to Yukon.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201129124348if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates
column36: As classes have been suspended until the end of the academic year and children have been learning from home, the Government of Yukon announced on 19th May that to offset costs incurred as a result of students learning from home, families with children in Kindergarten to Grade 12 who have been impacted by Covid-19 may apply for a one-time $250 CAD payment for each student. It is not said how much money is expected to be spent by the Government on this, but the article does state that there are 5,610 school students in Kindergarten to Grade 12 (as of 31st March), suggesting that this scheme may cost up to $1,402,500 CAD.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201206163652/https://yukon.ca/en/news/government-yukon-offering-support-families-impacted-covid-19

On 20th May, the Government of Yukon announced the extension of the Business Relief Program from 22nd May, to 23rd July. The source below states that as of 19th May, over $1.6 million CAD worth of support for businesses has been approved under this programme (note that the amount expected to be spent on the programme has already been included in a data note on 9th April). The Government of Yukon does not state how much extra the programme is expected to cost as a result of its extension.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201206164526if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/government-yukon-extends-support-yukon-businesses

On 22nd May, the Government of Yukon announced the Staffing Up labour market funding programme, which will receive $750,000 CAD ($534821.18 USD) to be used to encourage Yukon employers who offer critical and essential services to create new summer jobs for graduating and postsecondary level students.    Also on 22nd May, the Government of Yukon announced a programme to provide low-paid essential workers income support of up to $4 CAD per hour to a maximum of $20 per hour for up to 16 weeks. To receive this support, the worker's base wage must be no more than $20 per hour. If eligible, workers will receive a top-up of either $4 per hour or an amount that brings their wage to $20 per hour (depending on which is less). The Government of Yukon did not say how much this programme will cost.    Sources:   https://web.archive.org/web/20201025044013if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/funding-help-yukon-employers-hire-students-critical-and-essential-services  https://web.archive.org/web/20201206165208if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/essential-workers-receive-income-support-government-yukon

column12: It was announced on May 22nd that from 27th May, personal services businesses (including hair salons, barber shops, tattoo parlours, nail salons and non-registered massage therapists) are allowed to reopen so long as they had a government-approved COVID-19 operational plan.    Restaurants, bars, and public pools remain closed at this time (though restaurants can still provide take-out and deliveries).    Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20201117170903if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates

Bars and public pools remain closed.     However, restaurants (which were previously only allowed to operate take-out and deliveries) can reopen on 29th May, so long as they have a government-approved Covid-19 operational plan too protect staff and customers. The Government update on 12th June (also in the source referenced below) indicates that when restaurants reopened for business on 29th May, they could only operate at 50% of capacity.    Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20201117170903if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates

column32: The Canada Emergency Response Benefit (CERB) provided financial support to employed and self-employed Canadians who were directly affected by COVID-19. column36: On 2nd June, the Government of Yukon announced that Disability Services families would receive extra funding of $250 to $400 per month from June until August to help support them during the pandemic because of the fewer services available to them in the community.     The Government of Yukon does not state how much this will cost. However, the  source referenced below states that there are 221 families using Disability Services and 22 Approved Home Caregivers. With an extra $400 a month being offered to the former and an extra $250 a month being offered to the latter, the programme can be expected to cost a maximum of $93,900 CAD ($69,464.79 USD).    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201206174321if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/disability-services-families-receive-additional-support

column52: June 3    Today, the Minister of Transport, the Honourable Marc Garneau, announced he is expanding the requirements for the use of face coverings by workers and others involved in the transportation system, to reduce the risk of COVID-19.    https://web.archive.org/web/20201118161447/https://www.canada.ca/en/transport-canada/news/2020/06/minister-garneau-announces-new-measures-for-the-use-of-face-coverings-in-the-canadian-transportation-sector.html

column36: On 4th June, the Government of Yukon announced supports for restaurants and other businesses with a liquor license, who will receive a 25% discount off of the retail price for liquor, applicable only for the time that restaurants can open at 50% capacity only (starting from 29th May). These licensees will also be refunded 50% of this year’s licence fee as they've had to close for a period during Yukon's Covid-19 response. The Government of Yukon does not state how much these supports are expected to cost them.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201206175653if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/support-restaurants-announced

column43: The following document (published on March 23rd but updated on June 6th) is the Yukon Government's guidance to Whitehorse on Covid-19 testing criteria, explaining it in depth.     It explains that those tested should have any of the following symptoms (if returned from travel outside Yukon within the last 14 days, or had close contact with someone within the last 14 days who has): fever and/or chills, cough, difficulty breathing, sore throat or hoarse voice, headache, unexplained runny nose or nasal congestion, unexplained gastrointestinal symptoms (e.g. vomiting or diarrhoea), fatigue/muscle aches, loss of sense of taste and/or smell.    Those who have not travelled outside Yukon in the last 14 days (or had close contact in the last 14 days with someone who has, but has a fever and/or chills, a cough, or difficulty breathing can also be tested.    Finally, anyone hospitalised with lower respiratory illness can receive a Covid-19 test.    Sources:   https://web.archive.org/web/20200906165212/https://yukon.ca/sites/yukon.ca/files/covid-19_testing_recommendations_2020-06-05-_whitehorse_final.pdf

column15: The policy remains that no more than 10 people can attend a single gathering.     However, from 7th June, an exception is made for faith-based services.  From this date, places of worship will be allowed to open, with social distancing measures in place. These may involve operating at 1/3rd of capacity, up to a maximum of 50 people. Sanitation measures must also be in place, so cleaning and disinfection of common, high-touch areas should be more frequent. An operational plan needs to be in place.    Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20201117170903if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates

column29: June 8, 2020: The Canada Border Services Agency announced that as of June 8, 2020 23:59 EDT, foreign nationals who are immediate family members of Canadian citizens and permanent residents, and who do not have COVID-19 or exhibit any signs or symptoms of COVID-19, or who do not have any reason to believe they have COVID-19, will be exempt from the prohibition on entry to Canada if entering to be with an immediate family member for a period of at least 15 days    See this as essentially still a full border closure as no commercial flights operating unless in these specific circumstances for individuals who are family members.    https://web.archive.org/web/20201203160259/https://www.mccarthy.ca/en/insights/articles/covid-19-emergency-measures-tracker    https://web.archive.org/web/20201203160259/https://www.canada.ca/en/border-services-agency/news/2020/06/changes-to-travel-restrictions-for-immediate-family-members-of-canadian-citizens-and-permanent-residents.html

column12: On 11th June, the Government of Yukon announced the reopening of recycling services, which had been closed since 30th March. Free stores however, remain closed.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201206180620if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/recycling-services-resume-across-yukon
column34: On 11th June, a Ministerial Order was signed that protected tenants who either has to follow a Covid-19 health-protection measure after 25th June, or  who owe back rent as a result of losing income due to Covid-19 between 26th March and 25th June. The Order prevents a landlord from evicting a tenant who has breached the tenancy agreement or the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act as a result of the tenant following a health-protection order.    The Order also allows tenants who have rent arrears as a result of them following  a health-protection order after 25th June, to pay before December 31st. If a tenant owes rent from 26th March to 25th June as a result of them, or a household member following a health-protection measure, or due to loss of income as a result of Covid-19, they must also pay the rent owed before 31st December.    Source: https://archive.vn/jPatg    http://web.archive.org/web/20201206182335/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/economic-and-social-supports-covid-19/paying-rent-loans-or

column58: From 12th June, outdoor visits for long-term care residents are now allowed. Residents can identify one visitor with whom they can visit in a pre-set outdoor location.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201129124348if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates

column21: An update on 18th June confirms that bus capacity for Whitehorse's transit system (the only inner-city bus system in Yukon) remains limited to 12 passengers.     Source:   https://web.archive.org/web/20201120114631/https://www.whitehorse.ca/Home/Components/News/News/4531/31
column36: On 18th June, the Government of Yukon announced $1,633,365 CAD ($1,201,545.87 USD) of funding for territorial sport organisations, special recreation groups, athletes and officials.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201206181232if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/government-yukon-provides-more-16-million-funding-territorial-sport-and-recreation
column41: From as early as 18th June, the Government of Yukon created a website with extensive information on Covid-19. This includes information on borders and travel, childcare and education, economic and social supports, operating guidelines for industry and events, critical and essential services, general Covid-19 restrictions updates and information on health and Covid-19 (symptoms, steps to take to stay safe, etc.)    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20200618084410if_/https://yukon.ca/en/covid-19-information

column12: Announced on 12th June by the Government of Yukon, as of 19th June, bars can reopen at 50% capacity, provided they have an operational plan, approved by the Health Emergency Operations Centre.  Live music is prohibited and recreation activities including dart boards, pool tables, dance floors and gaming (such as pinball and video games) cannot be used.    However, public pools are still required to close.    Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20201117170903if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates

column9: Phase 2 of the Yukon plan for lifting Covid-19 restrictions (from 1st July - 31st July) allowed for the resumption of in-person K-12 education for the 2020-2021 school year. However, this school year does not start until 20th August and the 2019-20 year ended in roughly mid-June. So in Phase 2, public schools remained closed in Yukon.    Sources:   http://web.archive.org/web/20201117155139if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/summary-yukons-plan-lifting-covid-19-restrictions    http://web.archive.org/web/20200801060531/https://yukon.ca/sites/yukon.ca/files/edu/edu-school-calendar-important-dates-2019-2020.pdf
column12: On 1st July, restaurants can now operate at 100% capacity (they could previously only operate at 50% capacity). This announcement was made on 17th June.    On 24th June, the Government of Yukon announced that from 1st July, public pools can reopen so long as they have secured an approved Operational Plan and have subsequently been inspected.    With the reopening of public pools, there are no more requirements for businesses of any sector to close. However, there remain restrictions on businesses. The businesses previously required to close need to submit an operational plan to be approved in order for them to open. All other businesses, service providers and employers are required to have implemented a COVID-19 operational plan, and though it does not need to be submitted for approval, these businesses should be prepared to provide it for inspection by the government if requested.    Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20201117170903if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates
column18: From 1st July, the maximum number of people attending an outdoors gathering increased to 50 people.  Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201114230207/https://yukon.ca/sites/yukon.ca/files/cs/cs-cema-ministerial-authorization-outdoor-gatherings-up-to-50-people-june-18-2020.pdf
column27: The Government of Yukon announced on 24th June that from 1st July, British Columbia and Yukon residents will be allowed to travel between the two states without having to undergo 14 days self-isolation.    It was also announced that from 1st July, Northwest Territories and Nunavut residents will be able to enter Yukon without having to undergo 14 days self-isolation, but only if they travel directly to Yukon from Northwest Territories or Nunavut or via British Columbia.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201129124348if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates
column52: As of 1st July, (non-medical) masks must be worn in all Yukon airports. These masks should follow guidelines including: fitting securely with ties/ear loops; being changed asap if damp or dirty; being comfortable and not requiring frequent adjustment; being made of at least two layers of tightly woven material; fully covering the nose and mouth without leaving gaps.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201120235009if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/non-medical-masks-now-required-all-yukon-airports

column36: On 10th July, the Government of Yukon announced that its Rent Assist programme would be extended. The source referenced below states the programme's budget is $1.29 million CAD ($949,061.79 USD). Please note that whilst the programme has been previously mentioned in a data note on 11th May, at the time, the Government did not state how much it would cost, so the full cost of the programme has been included here.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201206183921if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/support-program-help-yukoners-pay-rent-extended

column43: On 15th July, the Government of Yukon announced an expansion of its testing criteria to include those with no recent travel history outside of Yukon but whose symptoms are among those in the following list: fever, chills, cough, shortness of breath, runny nose, sore throat, loss of sense of taste or smell, headache, fatigue, loss of appetite, nausea and vomiting, diarrhoea and muscle aches.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201206185432if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/expanded-testing-criteria-covid-19

column45: A Government of Yukon update on 22nd July confirmed that contact tracing is underway and anyone named as a contact of a confirmed Covid-19 case will be contacted by Yukon Communicable Disease Control.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201201112114if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates

column9: Schools remain closed (for the summer break), but it had been announced in July's Phase 2 of the Yukon plan for lifting of Covid-19 restrictions that schools would reopen for the 2020-21 school year (starting on 20th August). This policy remains unchanged.    Sources:  http://web.archive.org/web/20201117155139if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/summary-yukons-plan-lifting-covid-19-restrictions    http://web.archive.org/web/20200801060531/https://yukon.ca/sites/yukon.ca/files/edu/edu-school-calendar-important-dates-2019-2020.pdf    http://web.archive.org/web/20201117154845/https://yukon.ca/en/school-holiday-dates
column15: As of 1st August, 50 people can attend an "organised, seated events occurring in a rental or public facility or venue" indoors, and 100 people can attend this outdoors.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201114230851/https://yukon.ca/sites/yukon.ca/files/cs/cs-cema-ministerial-authorization-gatherings-up-to-100_people-aug-4-2020.pdf

column36: On 5th August, the Government of Yukon announced that support for restaurants would be extended until 1st November. Businesses with a liquor licence will continue to receive a 25% discount on the retail price of liquor.    Source:  https://web.archive.org/web/20201206190517if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/support-restaurants-extended

column52: On 12th August, the Chief Medical Officer for Health recommended to the Department of  Education that children over ten wear (non-medical) masks where social distancing cannot be  maintained (e.g. on school buses). Sources: https://web.archive.org/web/20201120112503/https://www.whitehorse.ca/residents/covid-19    https://web.archive.org/web/20201120122042/https://www.yukon-news.com/news/families-face-challenges-in-getting-students-to-and-from-school/

column36: On 24th August, the Government of Yukon announced that they would invest $2,438,750 million CAD ($1,844,857.72 USD) in three infrastructure projects to support communities and the economy. The projects they are investing in are intended to create jobs and improve Yukoners' quality of life.     These projects are:   1. Building the Tr’ondëk Hwëch’in Youth Centre in Dawson.  2. Upgrading and expanding the sewage lagoon in Carcross to provide cleaner water. A new lift station will also be constructed in Carcross.   3. The administrative building in Watson Lake will be fit with upgrades to improve energy efficiency.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201206231633if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/canada-and-yukon-invest-infrastructure-support-communities-and-economy

On 23rd September, the Government of Yukon announced that funding for the fall intake of the Advanced Artist Award program increased by $75,000 CAD ($56,092.43 USD) to a total of $150,000 CAD.     Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201206234035if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/funding-advanced-artist-award-doubled

column45: A Government of Yukon update on 30th September confirmed that as soon as Yukon Communicable Disease Control learns of a positive Covid-19 test they initiative contact tracing, speaking with the individual, their family and close contacts to establish their risk of having caught Covid-19.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201201112114if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates

column36: On 19th October, the Government of Yukon announced a new funding package for the tourism sector, the Tourism Accommodation Sector Supplement, given the serious effects Covid-19 has had on the sector. It will cost up to $2.88 million CAD ($2,189,357.27 USD) and will be part of the Yukon Business Relief Program.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201101004832if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/new-funding-package-announced-tourism-industry-hard-hit-covid-19

On 1st April (as recorded in a previous note), the Government of Yukon announced the Temporary Support for Events Funding Program, to help businesses recover specific costs where major events have had to be cancelled due to Covid-19 . The costs of this were not specified at the time. However in the Government of Yukon’s Economic Resilience Plan, published in March 2021, it was mentioned that as of 30th October 2020, the program approved $1,872,866 CAD ($1404497.95 USD) in compensation to 43 businesses for 31 cancelled events.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20210323212612/https://yukon.ca/sites/yukon.ca/files/economicresilienceplan_en_march11_102021_finalweb.pdf

column52: The Chief Medical Officer of Health has said that for Halloween, children should wear non-medical face masks or coverings.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201130115233if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/september-30-2020-covid-19-update

column36: On 9th November, the Government of Yukon announced a new support package for the aviation industry so that it can continue providing essential services to and from the territory and its remote communities. Air North will receive up to $5.7 million CAD. Alkan Air will receive up to $300,000 CAD. Charter and rotary carriers may receive up to $1.1 million CAD to support essential service operations. This amounts to a total of $7.1 million CAD ($5,470,890.88 USD) to be spent by the Government of Yukon in support of the aviation industry.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201207002813if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/new-support-yukons-aviation-industry

On 10th November, the Government of Yukon announced that funding for the Yukon Permanent Art Collection would increase by $30,000 CAD ($23076.84 USD) to $60,000 CAD, in order to provide greater support to Yukon-based artists.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201207003744if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/funding-doubled-annual-call-submissions-yukon-permanent-art-collection

column18: Policy remains unchanged.   Gatherings of 10 people can occur indoors,  50 people outdoors, with 2m social distancing between guests not in the same bubble.  Organised gatherings ("defined as seated events in a rented venue") can host 50 people indoors. These gatherings can host 100 people outdoors, with social distancing.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201103011306if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/holding-gathering-guidelines-covid-19

column58: On 17th November, restrictions were further eased for visitors to long term care facilities in the Yukon. Residents are now allowed to have four people on their visitor list, however visitors are still limited to two at a time and then only if they’re in the same social bubble.    Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20210218163620/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates

column27: It was announced on 18th November that as of 5pm on 20th November, all those entering Yukon must undergo 14 days self-isolation. This now includes those arriving from British Columbia,  Nunavut and the Northwest Territories.    Exceptions are made for critical service workers, those travelling from border areas, and those exercising an Aboriginal or treaty right (but this exception can be made for them only for the time needed to exercise that right).    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201129124348if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates

column43: A drive-through Whitehorse testing centre opened on 23rd November for "anyone who is experiencing any symptoms of COVID-19", confirming that this policy remains in place.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201201105620if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/whitehorse-covid-19-screening-drive-thru-opens
column52: As of 23rd November, face masks must be worn on Whitehorse public transit  (the only inner-city public transit system in Yukon). A few exceptions are made for: those with an underlying medical condition or disability which prevents them from wearing a mask; anyone unable to wear or remove a mask without help; children under 5; police or first responders during an emergency.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201130113621/https://www.whitehorse.ca/Home/Components/News/News/4618/31?backlist=%2F

column36: On 24th November, the Government of Yukon announced that the Yukon Essential Workers Income Support Program will be extended to 15th February, 2021. The Government of Yukon does not mention how much this program extension will cost. From the program's inception until 24th November, more than $1.2 million CAD ($921,075.85 USD) had been spent on the program. Please note: as it was not known how much would be spent on the programme at its inception on May 22nd, this spending was not accounted for in the corresponding data note and so has been included in this one instead.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201207005328if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/yukon-essential-workers-income-support-program-extended

column52: As of 26th November, face masks must be worn in all Yukon hospitals.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201130111333if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/your-health-covid-19/wearing-non-medical-masks-yukon

column36: On 30th November, the Tourism and Culture Minister announced the Tourism Non-Accommodation Sector Supplement, which will provide $1 million CAD ($770,488.61) of funding. Yukon tourism operators and food and beverage businesses who rely on visitors for at least 60% of their revenues can apply to the fund to break even, so long as they cannot obtain any further support from the Yukon Business Relief Program and CanNor’s Northern Business Relief Fund.    Also announced on 30th November was the Culture and Tourism Non-Profit Sector Supplement, for which $300,000 CAD ($231,146.58 USD) has been made available. Those eligible to apply are organisations which project year-end deficits which amount to over 10% of their operating budget.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201207013432if_/https://yukon.ca/en/news/additional-relief-funding-available-tourism-sector-and-non-profit-organizations

column52: As of 1st December, it is now mandatory to wear a face mask in all indoor public spaces in Yukon.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201201103146if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/your-health-covid-19/wearing-non-medical-masks-yukon

column32: The paid sick leave rebate programme remains in place until March 31st 2021.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20201207015633if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/economic-and-social-supports-covid-19/paid-sick-leave#apply-for-a-paid-sick-leave-rebate-for-employers

column34: The Ministerial Order from 11th June still applies. This Order protects tenants who either has to follow a Covid-19 health-protection measure after 25th June, or who owe back rent as a result of losing income due to Covid-19 between 26th March and 25th June. The Order prevents a landlord from evicting a tenant who has breached the tenancy agreement or the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act as a result of the tenant following a health-protection order.    The Order also allows tenants who have rent arrears as a result of them following a health-protection order after 25th June, to pay before 31st December. If a tenant owes rent from 26th March to 25th June as a result of them, or a household member following a health-protection measure, or due to loss of income as a result of Covid-19, they must also pay the rent owed before 31st December.    Source: https://archive.vn/jPatg    http://web.archive.org/web/20201206182335/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/economic-and-social-supports-covid-19/paying-rent-loans-or

column27: On 22nd December, the Chief Medical Officer for Health announced new options for those visiting Yukon undergoing self-isolation in a household with others.     The update states that visitors do not need to socially distance within a household whilst they are undergoing 14 days self-isolation if the rest of the household are self-isolating with them. In this scenario, if the visitor in the household leaves Yukon before their 14-day isolation has come to an end, the rest of the household is allowed to end their self-isolation three days after their guest has left, so long as they monitor themselves and check in with their former guest to see if they have Covid-19 symptoms. If neither are symptomatic after three days, the household can end their self-isolation.    If however, while a household's guest is self-isolating, others in the household do not self-isolate themselves, the guest must socially distance at all times from the rest of the household at a distance of two metres.    Source: http://web.archive.org/web/20210103134028if_/https://yukon.ca/en/health-and-wellness/covid-19-information/latest-updates-covid-19/chief-medical-officer-of-health-covid-19-updates

column32: Initially coded by Femi Adebola. The Canada Emergency Wage Subsidy (CEWS) supports employers that are hardest hit by the pandemic, and protect the jobs Canadians depend on. The subsidy generally covers 75% of an employee's wages – up to $847 per week - for employers of all sizes and across all sectors who have suffered a drop in gross revenues of at least 15% in March, and 30% in April and May. The program will be in place for a 12-week period, from March 15 to June 6, 2020. Also, the Canadian government will provide a taxable benefit of $2,000 every 4 weeks for up to 16 weeks to eligible workers who have lost their income due to COVID-19 under the Canadian Emergency Response Benefit. (Recoded from 2A to 2F after 22 April 2021 discussion.) Archived: https://web.archive.org/web/20200318220215/https://www.canada.ca/en/department-finance/economic-response-plan.html

column36: Small Business and Community Support Measures:  Canada’s Regional Development Agencies (RDAs) are the front line for economic development in Canada and help to address key economic challenges by providing regionally tailored programs, services, knowledge and expertise. column60: Ontario Extends Infectious Disease Emergency Leave for Workers during COVID-19.     Terminations that are normally triggered when temporary layoffs exceed the permitted length under the Employment Standards Act can result in costly payouts which, for many businesses, could be the difference between survival and closure. Under the new regulatory change to the Employment Standards Act, non-unionized employees who have had their hours reduced or eliminated because of the pandemic will be deemed to be on Infectious Disease Emergency Leave. column9: Those students below the university level are broadly in school most days. Certain school boards are alternating online days for older students in hotspots like Quebec. Once again, most universities are operating online.     The province of Newfoundland and Labrador's only university, Memorial University, is operating online for example, meaning they have no in person university classes in the province. Although most universities are technically doing this of their own accord, almost every university in Canada is public and funded/deeply connected to their provincial governments. So, while many universities did this of their own accord, I've put T2 because of their strong links to the government, and preemptive action negated a need to pass laws. In short, there is no reason for certain provinces to pass legislation, because these shut downs have already been done, likely in consultation with the provincial governments. The fact stands that there are entire provinces which do not have in person learning at the university level. Hence T2.     The entire decision making process is happening at a very decentralized level, happening in individual universities within distinct provinces. It is not generally closed however, since certain universities are doing in person classes. One example of this is St Xavier University in Nova Scotia (a smaller liberal arts university). column24: Manitoba, 12 Nov 2020:   Premier Brian Pallister and Dr. Brent Roussin, Manitoba’s chief provincial public health officer, announced that as of 12:01 a.m. on Thursday, Nov. 12, the province of Manitoba will move to the Critical level (red) on the #RestartMB Pandemic Response System to halt COVID-19 transmission and protect Manitoba’s most vulnerable citizens. “We are at a critical point in our fight against COVID-19, and we must do everything we can to protect our most vulnerable Manitobans and ensure our health-care system is there for Manitobans, when they need it,” said Pallister. “This is a team effort, and we all have a role to play in protecting ourselves, our loved ones and our community. By taking these measures seriously, we are going to save lives.” The new Critical (red) level restrictions will be in effect provincewide and include: • Social contacts reduced to your household only. Social gatherings are not permitted. • Travel to and from northern Manitoba is restricted and non-essential travel is discouraged. • Retail businesses listed as critical services, such as grocery stores and pharmacies, can remain open at 25 per cent capacity. • Retail businesses not on the list are able to provide e-service, curbside pickup or delivery services. • All personal service businesses, including hair salons, barbers and sites offering manicures, pedicures and other esthetic services, must close. • Gyms and fitness centres must close. • Religious and cultural gatherings must close or be provided virtually only. • Restaurants must close to the public and may be open for delivery, drive-thru or takeout only. • All recreational activities, sports facilities, casinos, museums, galleries, libraries, movie theatres and concert halls must close. https://web.archive.org/web/20201129151218/https://news.gov.mb.ca/news/index.html?item=49737    Nunavut, 12 Nov 2020:   On 12th November, after one positive Covid-19 case was found in Rankin Inlet, adding to the two confirmed cases in Sanikiluaq, Nunavut's Chief Public Health Officer asked the populations of Rankin Inlet and Sanikiluaq to "Stay home and stay safe" and "Do not travel if it isn’t necessary – now is not the time." column29: The federal government announced the following changes going into effect on 15 June 2020 (see http://web.archive.org/web/20200621201206/https://www.sem.admin.ch/sem/en/home.html)    "From 15 June, border controls at all land and air borders between Switzerland and the other Schengen states will be lifted. From then, normal entry requirements will apply again:  to all citizens of a Schengen state  to persons with rights of free movement  to third-country nationals who do not require a visa who are already legally resident in the Schengen area"    However: "Foreign nationals without rights of free movement who wish to enter Switzerland but do not fall within any of the categories of exceptions under the  COVID-19 Ordinance are still subject to entry restrictions." whereby "right of free movement" is defined as "EU/EFTA and UK citizens and their family members, irrespective of their nationality, have rights of free movement. Family members are defined as spouses and relatives in descending line (i.e. children and grandchildren, etc., including those of the spouse) who are under the age of 21 years or who are dependent, and dependent relatives of the person concerned or his or her spouse in ascending line (i.e. parents, grandparents). Different rules apply for students’ family members). Third-country nationals also have rights of free movement if they are posted to work in Switzerland for no more than 90 days by an employer based in the EU/EFTA, provided they have previously been living and working legally in an EU/EFTA member state for at least one year."    Therefore: despite the big change since 15 June 2020, the flag needs to be kept at "3-Ban" as some people who want to visit Switzerland but do not fall into the "right of free movement description" are still banned entry (e.g. tourists from outside of EU/EFTA/UK).

column12: ** At the federal level:  Effective on 22 June 2020: "Since 22 June the recommendation to work from home and specific requirements for protecting people at especially high risk have been lifted. Employers may now decide themselves how to protect their employees and whether they should work from home or in the office.  The Employment Act applies in all cases: employers are required to protect the health of their employees with appropriate measures. With regard to the coronavirus, this means that employers must ensure that their employees can observe the recommendations on hygiene and social distancing. If it is not possible to respect the recommended distance, measures should be introduced that apply the usual workplace STOP principle (Substitution, Technical measures, Organisational measures, Personal protective equipment). column9: FOR PRIMARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOL: C1=0  Except for canton Tessin, all Summer recesses ended on 26 August 2020 and all schools are open for face-to-face education, with hygiene measures defined by the canton. In case of infections, individual people or groups that were in contact with the infected person need to go in quarantine but entire schools have not been closed, so that C1=0 seems to describe the situation best    DETAILS on cantons 01-08 (the next sets of cantons will be checked during a later update in a cyclical manner)    01 Zürich: "All school levels start with whole classes in the 2020/21 school year. The schools have drawn up protection concepts... At grammar schools and vocational schools, pupils are now wearing masks outside of class in the interior of the school."  (http://web.archive.org/web/20200826184100/https://www.zh.ch/de/gesundheit/coronavirus/informationen-rund-um-schulen-kitas-heime.html)  No information could be found on school closures.    02 Bern: "Face-to-face teaching with protective measures"  (http://web.archive.org/web/20200826184719/https://www.erz.be.ch/erz/de/index/kindergarten_volksschule/kindergarten_volksschule/corona/schuljahr-2020-21.assetref/dam/documents/ERZ/AKVB/de/00_Allgemeines/allgemeines_volksschule_corona_leitfaden_praesenzunterricht_mit_schutzmassnahmen_d.pdf)  No information could be found on school closures.    03 Luzern: "Classes take place regularly in full classes. It is important to adhere to the hygiene and distance rules.§  (http://web.archive.org/web/20200826184941/https://volksschulbildung.lu.ch/coronavirus)  No information could be found on school closures.    04 Uri: Fact-to-face teaching with hygiene measures (http://web.archive.org/web/20200520085202/https://www.ur.ch/publikationen/20342)  No information could be found on school closures.    05 Schwyz:  "The education department of the canton Schwyz has determined that the resumption of school operations after the summer holidays should take place at all schools in face-to-face classes. Depending on the school level, different protection concepts are used - but what they all have in common is that there is no general mask requirement in class." (http://web.archive.org/web/20200826185952/https://www.sz.ch/public/upload/assets/48071/MM_Schulstart_SJ2020_21_Schutzkonzepte.pdf)  Some people need to go into quarantine due to local infections but entire schools were not closed.    06 Obwalden: "The new school year starts with classroom and full-class lessons. The hygiene and protective measures introduced by the FOPH before the summer holidays apply to primary schools. Each school has created its own protection concept. There is no general mask requirement." (http://web.archive.org/web/20200826162758/https://www.ow.ch/de/verwaltung/dienstleistungen/?dienst_id=5962)  The strategy is to impose quarantine for the people who had contact to a confirmed case but not to close schools. This happened on 26 August 2020 in a school in Sachseln (http://web.archive.org/web/20200826191142/https://www.pilatustoday.ch/zentralschweiz/luzern/nach-corona-fall-50-sachsler-oberstufenschueler-in-quarantaene-138902006)    07 Nidwalden: face to face education with hygiene measures (http://web.archive.org/web/20200826191603/https://www.nw.ch/_docn/223337/FAQ_Schulstart_Schuljahr_2020.pdf)  No information could be found on school closures.    08 Glarus: "In the 2020/21 school year, lessons at the Glarus schools will take place at all levels in all subjects and in all lessons according to the timetable. The necessary protective and preventive measures continue to apply" (http://web.archive.org/web/20200826191948/https://www.gl.ch/verwaltung/finanzen-und-gesundheit/gesundheit/coronavirus.html/4817)  No information could be found on school closures. column32: On December 18, 2020, the parliament agreed on an additional article in the Covid-19 law. column62: Priority list updated on 30 December 2020:    Who is to be vaccinated?  The plan is to prioritise vaccination of target groups of people age 16 as follows:    Target group 1: People at especially high risk (vulnerable people; excluding pregnant women)  Target group 2: Healthcare professionals with patient contact/carers for people at especially high risk  Target group 3: Close contacts (household members) of people at especially high risk  Target group 4: People in communal facilities with an increased risk of infection and outbreaks (for example homes for the handicapped).  Given that as vaccination starts there are not sufficient doses of vaccine available, further prioritisation is necessary within target group 1.    The following people are to be given access to vaccinations first:    People age 75 and over  People with chronic diseases of the highest risk, regardless of their age  After that come:    People aged between 65 and 74  People under 65 and people with chronic diseases who have not yet been vaccinated    Following people in target group 1, the vaccination will be offered to people in target groups 2, 3 and 4 in that order. In due course adults who are not in target groups 1 to 4 will also be able to have the vaccination.    It is not yet planned to vaccinate children. Study data for the relevant age groups is not yet available.    https://web.archive.org/web/20201231115345/https://www.bag.admin.ch/bag/en/home/krankheiten/ausbrueche-epidemien-pandemien/aktuelle-ausbrueche-epidemien/novel-cov/impfen.html

column62: In collaboration with Chile’s Advisory Committee on Vaccination and Immunization (Comité Asesor en Vacunación e Inmunizaciones, CAVEI), the Ministry of Health released provisional recommendations for initial prioritization of groups to be vaccinated. The recommendations split the vaccination campaign into three phases.     https://web.archive.org/web/20201226224848/https://www.minsal.cl/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/CAVEI-Priorizacion-grupos-vacuna-COVID19_ENMIENDA-22dic2020.pdf     1a)  Clinical and administrative health personnel in open, closed and emergency care, who includes: clinical services (includes dental), clinical support services (laboratory, radiology, pharmacy, pathological anatomy), administrative, food, transport, security, cleanliness.    Students of careers in the health areas in clinical practice.    1b) People residing in long-stay centers, in SENAME1 centers or in an agreement with that institution, in mental health care institutions and people deprived of Liberty    1c) Critical staff of the State Administration, Forces of Order and Security, Armed Forces deployed in the action plan for coronavirus, Gendarmerie, Firemen.    2a) People over 65    2b) Person with comorbidities    3a) Personnel in basic and essential services, such as electricity, water, gas, power generation, fuels, telecommunications, waste collection, landfills.    Personnel who perform functions in ONEMI and CONAF. FONASA and Civil Registry service personnel. Personnel transport personnel: metro, public locomotion drivers and railways. Personnel transporting critical supplies, such as food, clinical supplies, medicines. Critical staff of Municipalities. Critical staff of the 23 ministries. Critical staff of the Judiciary. Critical staff of the Legislative Branch. Critical staff of Regional Governments.    3b)  Nursery staff. Kindergarten staff. Teachers of preschool, basic and secondary education.    3c) The general public     Personnel performing critical functions, and those essential for the direct attention of citizens has been coded as ‘frontline/essential workers.’ Workers in transport companies have been coded under ‘other high contact professions.’ Inmates and prisoners have been coded under the ‘crowded/communal living conditions’ category.

column58: 3G  The Ministry of Civil Affairs recently issued ‘The Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of COVID-19 in Elderly Care Facilities (Version One).’   The notice included 6 aspects of measures: organization and leadership, access management, psychological comfort, elderly protection, internal control, and common disinfectants. According to the guidelines, care facilities are required to 1) reduce entry and exit of people by banning some unnecessary visitors and recording information of necessary visitors, 2) quarantine returning workers and newly admitted elderly, 3) clean and sanitize daily, and 4) conduct temperature tests on elderly daily    https://web.archive.org/web/20200813142904/http://www.gov.cn/xinwen/2020-01/28/content_5472755.htm

On January 29, Hubei Provincial Civil Affairs Department announced that all LTCF for the elderly people should execute temporarily closed management, requring that:  1. Cancel all visits and gatherings. Relatives of their children are encouraged to use wechat, videos and phone calls to console the elderly. LTCFs are not allowed to accept new elderly residents before the epidemic is over.  2. Pay daily attention to the health conditions of elderly people. The body temperature of elderly people and staff should be measured twice a day; Windows should be opened regularly for ventilation, and hospital disinfection should be carried out regularly to maintain environmental hygiene in the institution.  3. Home care services for the elderly in urban and rural communities will be suspended. All home-based elderly care service organizations in the province should suspend door-to-door service projects for the elderly, and all street day care centers for the elderly, urban and rural community home care centers, meals for the elderly and other service facilities should be temporarily closed.  4. Strengthen personal protection for staff in elderly care institutions. Staff of institutions should strictly implement prevention and control systems such as disinfection and temperature measurement on their daily commute. Elderly care workers who have returned to work from middle-risk areas should be quarantined at home for 14 days.  https://archive.vn/n88Nr

column58: The Ministry of Civil Affairs has drawn up three guidelines for the use of local civil affairs departments to better prevent and control epidemic in elderly care institutions. column52: On March 18,  National Health Commission of the People's Republic of China issued a guidance on mask wearing. Medical masks and surgical masks are sufficient for normal use, and wearing multiple masks does not provide more protection, according to the guideline. The public is advised to carry along masks when in crowded places such as offices, shopping malls, restaurants, workshops and public transport. People in high-risk areas should wear surgical masks all the time when entering such places, while those in medium-risk and low-risk areas need to wear medical masks when in contact with others at the distance of less than 1 meter. Those who have cold symptoms such as coughing or sneezing, or who live with personnel in quarantine or that have recovered from the novel coronavirus and been discharged from the hospital, are suggested to wear disposable medical or surgical masks. People working in places such as hospitals, train terminals, airports, prisons and nursing homes need to wear surgical masks or respirators of grade KN95/N95 or above. The suspected cases, confirmed cases of novel coronavirus, asymptomatic cases and those who have close contact with confirmed cases are recommended to wear surgical masks or respirators with no breathing valve graded at KN95/N95 or above. Entry personnel need to wear such masks from the moment they enter the country to the end of their required quarantine.    See National Health Commission of the People's Republic of China website, archived:   http://archive.today/2020.10.19-223608/http://www.nhc.gov.cn/jkj/s3577/202003/0a472cc09e744144883db6a74fe6e760.shtml    See Zhejiang Daily website, archived:   https://web.archive.org/web/20210214055653/http://zjrb.zjol.com.cn/html/2020-03/19/content_3315711.htm?div=-1

column15: Measures announced on Sunday for the Tianshan district of Urumqi included mass health screenings, and some public transport and most flights into the city were stopped on Saturday. Group activities have been suspended and people were warned against unnecessary travel outside the city. District authorities have also “strengthened [housing] compound management”, including tighter controls over who goes in and out, carrying out a comprehensive disinfection of the public areas of the community, providing contactless delivery services and help purchasing daily necessities. Beijing, meanwhile, has gone 14 days without a case of local transmission, and city authorities on Sunday said they were downgrading the emergency response level from 2 to 3. The move is largely symbolic, with many measures remaining in place including mandatory social distancing, temperature checks and 14-day quarantines for passengers arriving from abroad.  https://web.archive.org/web/20210810021145/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jul/20/covid-19-outbreak-in-xinjiang-spreads-to-second-chinese-city

column55: This extended note aims to capture the progress on vaccination programme before it is rolled out to the entire country (does not include R&D, clinic trials).    The China National Medicine Products Administration (MPA) has not formally approved the Sinopharm Inactivated vaccine to go to the market. However, the green light is anticipated in the next few days.     http://web.archive.org/web/20201214212000/https://weareunited.com.my/11515744/    On 24 June 2020, the MPA approved the emergency use of COVID-19 vaccine. Voluntary vaccination started on around 17 June. The first batch of receivers consisted mainly of key workers, including state-owned enterprise employees who must go overseas to countries where the pandemic hits hard; medical staff, epidemic-control staff, border force and other essential workers who keep cities running.     http://web.archive.org/web/20201214231804/https://finance.sina.com.cn/chanjing/cyxw/2020-11-18/doc-iiznezxs2537217.shtml    From mid-October, Zhejiang province has offered vaccines to ordinary citizens on a voluntary basis. The rationale has been that many cities in Zhejiang have export-oriented economies; for example, Yiwu city is the world centre for light industry commodity trading. Many wholesale merchants were keen on receiving vaccines so that they can travel to Latin America and Africa to inspect their businesses. See BBC reports below. By mid-November, Zhejiang had provided vaccines to some 743,000 people. Voluntary vaccines were paid by recipients. Two doses cost roughly 400 CNY plus a service charge of around 56 CNY, which altogether equals to approximately 70 USD.     http://web.archive.org/web/20201214231741/https://www.bbc.com/zhongwen/simp/chinese-news-54628714    As the vaccination programme is yet to roll out to the whole country, there is no national policy on who will get the vaccine first. However, Sichuan province, where the most recent cluster of infection was found, did publish a detailed plan to that sets out the order:    The first group to receive vaccines consists of people facing high risks of infection, including medical staffs with International assistance mission, national health emergency rescue team in Sichuan, fever clinic and frontline doctors and nurses, border control force, frontline health inspection and epidemic-control officials, students or workers going overseas, police force, frozen food industry workers, essential workers for keeping cities running, teachers, other medical staffs, doctors and nurses, community social workers. The first batch is estimated to have 2 million people. Vaccination for them has started and will finish within 2020.    The second group to receive vaccines mainly consists of vulnerable people, including elderly people and people with chronic diseases. Vaccination for them will start from early next year (January).    The third batch will open to the general public. Ordinary people are estimated to start receiving vaccines after the Chinese New Year (12 February 2021).    http://web.archive.org/web/20201214221555/https://www.sohu.com/a/437018675_114988    So far, vaccination is not and is unlike to be paid by social medical insurance funds in the future. The National Health Security Administration has cited laws and regulations as the justification that vaccination is a part of public health effort, which should be shouldered by public finance resources, rather than social medical insurance funds.     http://web.archive.org/web/20201214211226/https://www.sohu.com/a/425495553_114986    UAE and Bahrain have formally approved the Sinopharm vaccine on 9th and 13th December 2020 respectively.    http://web.archive.org/web/20201214231619/http://www.xinhuanet.com/2020-12/09/c_1126842251.htm  http://web.archive.org/web/20201214231549/http://www.xinhuanet.com/world/2020-12/14/c_1126855787.htm

A:    China formally started to vaccinate group A - Key workers - and people who need to go to high-risk countries/regions to work and/or study on 15 Dec 2020. Key workers are those who work in frozen stuff-importing industry, border check, market for fresh meet and fish, public transportation, and hospital. Groups B and/or C will be the next to be vaccinated.    https://archive.vn/oG1an

column62: No published vaccination plan or strategy could be found for this time period on government websites or media reports.    On February 19th, 2021 Cote d'Ivoire's Director General of Health announced that the first shipment of vaccines through the COVAX facility would arrive by the end of the month. column34: https://web.archive.org/save/https://home.kpmg/xx/en/home/insights/2020/04/ivory-coast-government-and-institution-measures-in-response-to-covid.html    On 21 March 2020, the CBWAS took major measures, in order to mitigate the negative impact of the sanitary crisis:  A FCFA340bn financial help has been granted to commercial banks, so they can sustain the economy;  1,700 companies have been granted loans, while they were not eligible so far, so that they can benefit from further resources;  The West African Development Bank (WADB) will receive FCFA25bn from the CBWAS, in order to lower its interest rate and increase the amount of loans granted to WAMU members, so as to be able to fund the domestic economy;  To accept to delay financial debt reimbursements, especially for SMEs;  To decrease the cost of fund transfers through mobile money, in order to avoid a low in transactions;  To fund commercial banks with enough cash to guarantee a good working of cash machines;  If necessary, to reorganize the schedule of Treasury bills issuance.  The government announced several measures to preserve the key sectors of the economy:  The setting up of a private sector support fund for an amount of XOF 250 billion, in order to strengthen the SMEs with at least XOF 100 billion and the setting up of guarantee funds, in order to facilitate the access to bank credits;  The setting up of a specific support fund for informal sector enterprises affected by the crisis for an amount of XOF100 billion.  Support for the main sectors of the national economy, particularly cashew nuts, cotton, rubber, oil palm, cocoa and coffee with  XOF 250 billion;  Support for food, market gardening and fruit production for an amount of CFAF 50 billion, including CFAF 20 billion for inputs.
